head_text: The old seat of planetary government, a small city in the Imperial Basin under the Shield Wall. House Atreides lands here in the first book and holds the Residency until the Harkonnen night attack; Paul later makes it the capital of his empire.
Where the old Duke’s portrait and the head of the bull that killed him are hung. Duke Leto gives a dinner here for the planet’s powers, smugglers and Guild bankers among them.
The Residency’s great hall. After the battle Paul receives the defeated Emperor here, and kills Feyd-Rautha in single combat in front of the court.
Shaddam IV’s metal field shelter, set up among his ships on the landing field. The captive child Alia kills the Baron Harkonnen inside it.
A row of palms before the Residency, each drinking more water every day than a person needs to live: wealth on display in a thirsty city.

head_text: The Arrakeen residence designated for Duke Leto’s family, formerly the home of Count and Lady Fenring.

The landing field outside the city. The Atreides come down here from the Guild heighliner; before the final battle the Emperor’s frigates and the Harkonnen ships crowd onto it, and the worm-riders break in among them.
The crowded lanes where water-sellers ring their bells and cry their trade, and where water is money.
A district at the city’s edge where Paul’s old Fedaykin Otheym lives. Paul walks here at night disguised as a Fremen to see him.
The great rock wall that rises behind the city and shelters it from the storms of the open desert.
A cave in Habbanya Ridge, named on the map and used as a Fremen meeting place.
A cave in the ridge, named on the map.
A high bridge over the Idaho River on the royal road. When Leto’s wedding procession crosses it, the supports are cut and he falls into the river. Position estimated.
Where the dying God Emperor lies after the water has torn his body apart, telling Siona and Duncan the last secrets of the Golden Path.
The bridge the wedding procession crosses on the way to Tuono. The Fish Speaker Nayla cuts its supports with a lasgun and it falls.
The Harkonnen-built city about 200 kilometres northeast of Arrakeen across the Broken Land, larger and harsher than the old capital.
The Harkonnens’ city on Arrakis. When the Atreides take over the planet they choose to govern from smaller Arrakeen instead.
A broad low basin about 200 metres below the Bled.
A wide hollow in the desert floor, named on the map.
Leto II’s tower in the Sareer, the last desert on a green world, where the God Emperor keeps his court, his Duncan Idahos and his hidden spice. Position estimated.
The road along which the God Emperor’s great processions travel out to Onn and the villages.
The God Emperor’s seat in the middle of the Sareer. Leto dictates his journals here, talks for hours with his majordomo Moneo, and receives each new Duncan Idaho ghola.
The site on Rakis where Leto II’s hidden journals are later found, the record the fourth book presents itself as drawn from. Position estimated.
Where the God Emperor’s journals lay hidden until they were found, long after his death.
A sealed room in the ruins that Odrade, Sheeana and Waff reach by worm, holding words Leto II left for the far future.
One of the Imperial ecological testing stations, quietly used by Liet-Kynes and the Fremen. Paul and Jessica are brought here after their escape. Position estimated.
The hidden station itself; its layout here is schematic.
Paul and Jessica escape in an ornithopter and fly it into the heart of a sandstorm to shake off pursuit.
One of the rock walls in the desert that travellers mistake for the true Shield Wall.
A ridge of rock that looks like the Shield Wall from the sand.
The western of the two false walls that edge the Minor Erg.
The western false wall, at the edge of the Minor Erg.
Alia’s Fane, the great temple raised for Paul’s sister. In Children of Dune the blind Preacher is killed on its steps.
The square before the Fane, crowded with pilgrims of the Hajj. In Children of Dune the blind Preacher speaks here against the priesthood.
The heart of Alia’s temple, where pilgrims come to the holy sister of Muad’Dib.
The steps of Alia’s temple, where the Preacher is killed in front of the crowd.
The forest that walls off the Sareer from the green lands. Position estimated.
Where Siona’s rebels, carrying papers stolen from the Citadel, are hunted down by the God Emperor’s wolves. Only Siona gets away.
An open erg of shifting sand south of the Shield Wall, named on the book’s map.
An open sea of dunes where nothing stands still for long.
Open rock and sand south of the Wall. A line of outcrops runs from Sietch Tabr south towards the other sietch communities.
Rock outcrops running south from Sietch Tabr across the open flat, named on the map.
A long ridge deep in Fremen country, south and west of Sietch Tabr.
A long rock ridge in the deep desert, named on the map.
A pass through the Shield Wall. The map notes a shrine to Duke Leto’s skull overlooking it.
A way through the Shield Wall, named on the map.
The map’s notes place a shrine to the dead Duke’s skull above the pass.

A lost sietch of water-stealers in the deep desert, whose people were wiped out long ago and whose name the Fremen will not speak. Leto II flees here in Children of Dune and passes through the spice trance that sets him on the Golden Path. Position estimated.
The caves of the outcast sietch. Leto is taken captive here, and with Gurney Halleck watching he is forced into the spice trance and sees the Golden Path.
The city of the Priesthood of the Divided God on Rakis, on the ground of old Arrakeen and Onn. The Bene Gesserit keep a fortress here.
The Sisterhood’s fortress on Rakis, commanded by Darwi Odrade. Sheeana is brought here to be trained.
The pilgrims’ city that the Honored Matres burn when they scorch Rakis.
Where visitors come down to Rakis. In Heretics the Tleilaxu Master Waff arrives here, and later the Mother Superior Taraza herself.
The seat of the Priesthood of the Divided God and its High Priest Hedley Tuek, who rule Rakis in the name of the worms.
The immense palace Paul builds in Arrakeen as emperor, said to be the largest building ever raised. It is the setting of most of the second book.
Where the emperor receives embassies. The Guild Steersman Edric presents the ghola Hayt to Paul here; after Paul, Alia rules from the Keep.
Paul’s private rooms, which he shares with Chani, while his wife Irulan is kept apart from him.
The highest point of the Broken Land; the book’s map runs its zero meridian through this peak.
The highest point on the book’s map, from which its zero meridian is measured.
A deep cleft through the Shield Wall that the map credits to Paul, who blasted the Wall open with the house atomics so that the Fremen and their worms could ride into the Imperial Basin.
The cleft torn through the Shield Wall by the Atreides family atomics. Through it the Fremen ride their worms into the basin under cover of a great storm.
The festival city of the God Emperor, built where Arrakeen once stood. Leto comes here for the great festivals and audiences.
Where the powers of the empire keep their envoys to the God Emperor, the Ixian ambassador Hwi Noree among them.
Where the crowds gather when the God Emperor comes to Onn for his great festival.
Fremen plantings far in the southern desert, around 40 degrees south, where the hidden work of changing Arrakis is furthest along. Paul spends the later years of his desert war in the south.
Fremen plantings hidden far from Harkonnen eyes, where the long work of greening Arrakis has gone furthest.
Paul’s base in the later years of the desert war. He lies here for weeks in the trance of the Water of Life until Jessica and Chani wake him.
The low ground around the north pole, some 500 metres below the level of the Bled, near the small polar cap that the cities mine for water.
The planet’s small cap of ice, mined to water the cities of the north.
The deepest place on the map, more than 1,500 metres below the level of the Bled.
A rift cut far below the level of the desert floor.
A sheer scarp rising out of the western Shield Wall, one of the highest walls on the map.
A towering scarp of the western Shield Wall, named on the book’s map.
The only desert left in Leto’s time, a long strip of sand kept around the Citadel. Leto tests Siona by walking her across it. Position estimated.
The last true desert on Arrakis. Leto walks Siona and Duncan across it, and Siona must drink his spice essence to live.
A poor pan village in the open desert, destroyed by a sandworm that spared only one child, Sheeana, who can command the worms. Position estimated.
A hamlet on the open sand. A worm destroys it and leaves only the girl Sheeana alive, and the priests see her walk unharmed before the worms.
A great mountain wall around the northern lowlands that breaks the coriolis storms and shelters the cities. Beyond it lies the open desert of the Fremen.
South of the Wall the worms rule the sand, and only the Fremen live.
Sheer rock between the sheltered basin and the deep desert; the storms of the open sand break against it.
The hidden settlement in the deep desert where Jacurutu’s secret survivors live. Position estimated.
The secret warren of those who keep Jacurutu’s old ways alive.
A rock ridge in the desert south of the Wall, named on the map. Sihaya, the desert springtime, is also Paul’s private name for Chani.
A ridge of rock in the open desert, named on the map.

Stilgar’s sietch, a hidden cave-warren in the rock south of the Shield Wall. Paul and Jessica are taken in here; it becomes Paul’s base, Chani dies in childbirth here in the second book, and the twins grow up here.
Reservoirs of water the Fremen have hoarded for generations, saved toward Kynes’s dream of a green Arrakis. Paul is shown them in the first book.
The broken rock outside the sietch where the Corrinos’ tigers hunt Leto and Ghanima, who hide in a narrow crevice.
A concealed way into the rock, sealed against moisture loss.
The great cavern where the tribe gathers. Jessica drinks the Water of Life here before the assembled sietch and becomes the Fremen’s Reverend Mother.
The family’s rooms deep in the rock. Chani dies giving birth to the twins here, and Paul kills Scytale here.
Tuono Basin is named on the first book’s map. In God Emperor, Tuono is the village at the edge of the Sareer where Leto means to marry Hwi Noree. Position estimated.
A basin named on the first book’s map of the desert.
A village of museum Fremen, who act out the old desert life for the God Emperor. Duncan and Siona are sent here for safety, and Leto chooses it for his wedding.
A cliff-walled pass that opens onto the sink villages of the pyons.
A pass walled by cliffs, named on the map.
The sink villages of the pyons, the planet’s settled labourers, at the pass’s mouth.
The small Bene Gesserit station on Buzzell. Position estimated.
Where sisters out of favour are sent, and where the soostones the Honored Matres want are gathered from the sea.
The Atreides castle on the sea cliffs, Paul’s childhood home. Here the Reverend Mother Mohiam tests him with the gom jabbar. Position estimated.
Where Paul’s grandfather, the old Duke, was killed fighting a bull. The bull’s head and the old Duke’s portrait travel with the family to Arrakis.
The castle stands on cliffs above Caladan’s sea, the world of water the Atreides give up for a desert.
The ancient Atreides seat, home of the house for twenty-six generations. Before the move, the Reverend Mother Mohiam tests Paul here with the box of pain and the gom jabbar.
Where Gurney Halleck and Thufir Hawat drill Paul. Gurney teaches him to fight under a shield, where only the slow blade gets through.
Caladan’s lowland farms; pundi rice is its main export. Position estimated.
Flooded fields of pundi rice, the crop on which Caladan’s wealth rests.
The Sisterhood’s records, kept under Bellonda. Position estimated.
The Sisterhood’s records and its Mentat-archivist Bellonda, Odrade’s sharpest critic.
The main Keep of the Sisterhood and seat of the Mother Superior. Position estimated.
Chapterhouse’s orchards, which Odrade loves. In the last book they wither as the desert creeps in.
Where Murbella trains and the child Teg ghola is schooled as the Sisterhood’s next Bashar.
Odrade’s rooms high in Central, looking out over the orchards, where she plans the Sisterhood’s war and argues with Bellonda.
The spreading belt of sand where Sheeana tends the sandtrout and the first young worms. Position estimated.
Where farmland and orchards give way to sand as the desert spreads.
The belt of desert seeded by the sandtrout of the Rakis worm, where Sheeana watches for the first young worms.
Where the great no-ship rests, a prison for Duncan Idaho, Murbella and the Tleilaxu Master Scytale. Position estimated.
The landing field of Chapterhouse, where the Sisterhood’s ships come and go.
The ship Teg seized on Gammu, now grounded and hidden from prescient sight. Duncan, Murbella and the Master Scytale live aboard it as prisoners, and at the end it flies out into the unknown.

Duncan’s death — Duncan Idaho goads Stilgar into killing him, so that Stilgar must take Ghanima and flee Alia’s rule.
Leto and the Preacher — In the deep desert Leto finds the Preacher and knows him for his father, Paul, who could not walk the path that Leto has chosen.
Ghanima’s self-hypnosis — Ghanima puts herself into a trance so deep that she truly believes her brother was killed, so that no Truthsayer can uncover the lie.
Farad’n’s choice — Farad’n turns against his mother’s schemes, denounces her, and casts his lot with the Bene Gesserit.
The Corrino plot — On Salusa Secundus, Wensicia Corrino trains Laza tigers to kill the Atreides twins and clear the way for her son Farad’n.
The tigers — The twins survive the tigers. Leto lets it be believed he is dead and slips into the desert.
Jessica among the Corrinos — Duncan Idaho carries Jessica off to Salusa Secundus, where she trains Farad’n in the Bene Gesserit way.
Jacurutu and the Golden Path — Captured at Jacurutu, Leto is forced into the spice trance, sees the Golden Path, and covers himself in sandtrout, becoming more than human.
The Preacher’s death — The blind Preacher, who is Paul, is killed on the temple steps. Alia, possessed by the Baron, takes her own life when Leto confronts her.
The Preacher — A blind preacher out of the deep desert speaks to the pilgrim crowds against the priesthood that rules in Muad’Dib’s name. Some whisper that he is Paul.
Leto breaks the qanats — With the strength of his living skin, Leto runs across the desert and smashes the water channels of the terraforming to slow the death of the worms.
The gom jabbar — Before the move to Arrakis, the Reverend Mother Mohiam tests the fifteen-year-old Paul with a box of pain and a poisoned needle, and he passes.
The Emperor moves — With spice production collapsing, Shaddam IV, his Sardaukar and the Guild descend on Arrakis.
Battle of Arrakeen — Under cover of a great storm Paul blasts open the Shield Wall with the family atomics, and the Fremen ride worms into the Imperial Basin and overwhelm the Sardaukar.
Paul takes the throne — Paul kills Feyd-Rautha in single combat, forces the Guild to submit by threatening the spice, and claims the throne by agreeing to marry Princess Irulan.
Gurney’s lesson — Gurney Halleck spars with Paul in the castle’s training hall, teaching him that under a shield only the slow blade gets through.

The harvester and the worm — Watching the spice harvest from the air with Kynes, Duke Leto sees a worm coming for a crawler and orders the crew lifted out. He saves the crew and loses the machine, and the Fremen take note.

The Duke’s dinner — Leto gives a dinner for the powers of Arrakis, from a water-shipper and a Guild banker to the smuggler Esmar Tuek and Kynes himself. Talk of water and the plight of the Fremen runs under the courtesies.
Kynes in the desert — Left by the Harkonnens to die without a stillsuit in the open desert, Liet-Kynes dies dreaming of a green Arrakis as a spice blow erupts beneath him.
Usul — Taken in by Stilgar’s band, Paul kills Jamis in a ritual knife fight and becomes a Fremen. He takes the name Muad’Dib, after the desert mouse, while the tribe calls him Usul among themselves.
The Baron’s trap — Baron Harkonnen and Piter de Vries lay their plan: let the Atreides take Arrakis, then destroy them with a traitor inside their house and Sardaukar in Harkonnen uniform.
Gurney returns — Gurney Halleck, hiding among the smugglers, meets Paul again in the desert. Believing Jessica the traitor, he nearly kills her before Paul stops him.
The fleet on the plain — The Emperor’s ships and the Harkonnen forces crowd onto the plain below the Shield Wall, trusting the Wall to keep the desert out.
The raid on the sietch — Sardaukar raid a Fremen sietch. Paul’s infant son Leto is killed and Alia is taken captive.
Worms among the ships — The worm-riders burst onto the landing field among the Imperial and Harkonnen ships, and the Emperor’s army is broken.
Alia and the Baron — Brought before the Emperor as a captive, the child Alia stabs the Baron Harkonnen with a poisoned needle and kills him.
Thufir’s last refusal — Handed a poisoned needle and ordered to strike Paul, the old Mentat Thufir Hawat refuses and dies before the court.
A false scent — A Harkonnen plant points Thufir Hawat towards Jessica as the traitor in the house, hiding the real one, Dr Yueh.
Rabban’s squeeze — The Baron gives Arrakis to his brutal nephew Rabban to wring dry, meaning Feyd-Rautha to be welcomed later as the people’s deliverer.
Feyd’s failed plot — Feyd-Rautha’s attempt on his uncle’s life fails. The Baron punishes him by making him kill every woman of his pleasure wing.
In the stilltent — Hidden in a stilltent in the desert, Paul feels his mind open to the future and learns that his mother is a daughter of the Baron Harkonnen.
House Atreides comes to Arrakis — Duke Leto, Jessica and Paul come down at Arrakeen and take over the Residency. Leto sets out to win the Fremen and the planetologist Liet-Kynes.

Yueh’s betrayal and the night attack — Dr Yueh drops the house shields, and Harkonnen troops with disguised Sardaukar overrun Arrakeen. The captured Duke dies trying to kill the Baron with a poison tooth, killing Piter de Vries instead.
Flight into the deep desert — In the desert Paul and Jessica are taken to a hidden ecological testing station. Sardaukar attack; Duncan dies holding them off while Paul flies into a great storm.
Sietch Tabr — Jessica drinks the Water of Life and becomes the Fremen’s Reverend Mother, awakening her unborn daughter Alia. Paul takes Chani as his partner.
Paul rides the worm — Paul calls and rides his first sandworm, and his Fedaykin raids begin to cripple Harkonnen spice production.
Feyd-Rautha’s hundredth fight — On his birthday Feyd kills a captured Atreides fighter in the Harkonnen arena, while the Baron takes the captive Thufir Hawat into his service.
The Water of Life — Years later, in the south, Paul drinks the Water of Life, survives, and sees past and future at once: he is the Kwisatz Haderach.
The God Emperor — After three and a half thousand years Leto II has almost become a sandworm. He rules a peaceful, stagnant empire from his Citadel in the Sareer, guarded by his Fish Speakers.
Another Duncan — The Tleilaxu deliver the latest Duncan Idaho ghola to the Citadel. He wakes into a world thousands of years from his own, serving the grandson of the master he remembers.
Tuono — Moneo sends Duncan and Siona to the museum Fremen village of Tuono for their safety, and Leto moves his wedding there. There the two set aside their hatred and plan his death.
The last secret — Dying on the riverbank, Leto tells Siona that she is hidden from prescience, the true goal of his breeding, and that her descendants will be too.
Hwi Noree — Ix sends Hwi Noree as its ambassador. Leto falls in love with her and decides to marry her.
The test in the Sareer — Leto walks Siona and a Duncan ghola into the Sareer. To survive, Siona drinks his spice essence and sees the Golden Path, but keeps her resolve to kill him.
Festival at Onn — Leto holds his great festival in Onn, the city that rose on the ruins of Arrakeen.
The bridge over the Idaho River — On the way to his wedding, the Fish Speaker Nayla cuts the bridge. Leto falls into the river, and the water tears his body apart into sandtrout.
The hidden journals — Leto’s own record of his reign survives in hidden chambers on Arrakis, later found at Dar-es-Balat.
Wolves in the Forbidden Forest — Siona’s rebels flee through the Forbidden Forest with papers stolen from the Citadel. The God Emperor’s wolves run them down, and only Siona escapes.
Teg is called back — Mother Superior Taraza brings the old Bashar Miles Teg out of retirement to guard a new Duncan Idaho ghola.
The burning of Rakis — The Honored Matres attack Rakis and scorch its surface. Taraza and Waff die, and Teg dies in a last stand that draws the Matres in.
Attack on the Keep — Killers strike at the ghola inside Gammu Keep. Teg and Lucilla slip away with Duncan into the wild country.

Leto’s message — Riding a worm with Sheeana and the Tleilaxu Master Waff, Odrade reaches the ruins of Dar-es-Balat and finds a hidden room where Leto II left a message for those who would come after him.
The ghola on Gammu — Teg trains the young Duncan in the Bene Gesserit Keep, with the Imprinter Lucilla waiting to bind him to the Sisterhood.
Sheeana — A girl survives the worm that destroys her village on Rakis and is found to command the sandworms. The Bene Gesserit take her into their care.
Odrade on Rakis — Reverend Mother Darwi Odrade, Teg’s secret daughter, commands the Sisterhood’s keep at Keen and begins Sheeana’s training.
The Tleilaxu Masters — Tylwyth Waff and the Masters pursue their own plan against the Bene Gesserit and the returning Honored Matres.
The no-globe — Attacked on Gammu, Teg and Lucilla hide Duncan in an old Harkonnen no-globe, where Teg wakes Duncan’s original memories.

Teg breaks — Staying behind so Lucilla and Duncan can get away, Teg is taken by the Honored Matres and tortured with a T-probe. Something in him wakes: he moves faster than eyes can follow and fights his way out, then seizes a no-ship with veterans gathered in Ysai.
Duncan and Murbella — The Honored Matre Murbella tries to enslave Duncan sexually, but his Tleilaxu conditioning turns the bond on her, and all his past lives return to him.
Taraza and Waff — Taraza comes to Rakis to bargain with Waff, and plans for the planet’s destruction to serve the Sisterhood.
Scytale’s bargain — The Face Dancer Scytale offers to restore Chani as a ghola and threatens the newborn twins. Guided by his son’s eyes, Paul kills him.
Alia’s judgement — Alia has the conspirators put to death against Paul’s wishes, but spares Irulan, who gives up the Sisterhood to raise Paul’s children.
The false Lichna — The Face Dancer Scytale comes to Paul wearing the face of Otheym’s daughter Lichna, carrying a summons that draws the emperor into the conspirators’ trap.
The conspiracy — The Bene Gesserit, the Guild, the Tleilaxu and Princess Irulan join in a plot to bring down Emperor Paul.
Hayt — The Tleilaxu give Paul a ghola of Duncan Idaho, called Hayt, conditioned to kill him.
The stone burner — A forbidden atomic stone burner goes off in Arrakeen. Paul is blinded but goes on seeing through his prescience.
Chani dies — Chani dies giving birth to twins, Leto and Ghanima, which Paul had not foreseen. Hayt’s conditioning breaks and he becomes Duncan Idaho again.
Paul walks into the desert — Blind and without his vision, Paul follows Fremen custom and walks alone into the desert. Alia rules as regent.
The conquest of Naraj — Among the jihad’s battles is the taking of Naraj and its moons, where the defenders used a stone burner. The old Fedaykin Farok’s son lost his eyes there.
Otheym and the dwarf — Disguised as a Fremen, Paul walks into the city to visit the dying Fedaykin Otheym, who gives him the dwarf Bijaz, a living record of the names of traitors.
Chani and Irulan — Irulan has been secretly dosing Chani with a contraceptive to keep her from bearing Paul’s heir. When Chani changes her diet she conceives, but her body has been weakened.
Lampadas destroyed — The Honored Matres destroy the Bene Gesserit school world. Lucilla escapes carrying the memories of millions of Reverend Mothers.
The no-ship’s escape — Duncan, Sheeana, the Teg ghola, Scytale and the Jews fly the great no-ship out into the unknown with sandworms aboard, watched by a strange old couple, Daniel and Marty.
Prisoners of the no-ship — Duncan, Murbella and the Master Scytale live as prisoners aboard the grounded no-ship. Duncan keeps seeing an old man and woman in a shimmering net in his visions.
The desert grows — The worm’s sandtrout spread across Chapterhouse, killing its orchards and building a desert where Sheeana waits for new worms.
The child Bashar — A Teg ghola is grown and his memories awakened; Odrade makes him Bashar of the Sisterhood’s forces again.
Battle of Junction — Teg seizes Junction, but the Honored Matres turn the victory with a new weapon and capture Odrade.
The union — Murbella goes in among the Honored Matres, kills their new leader Logno, and is acclaimed by them; Odrade dies in the fighting. Murbella now heads both orders.
Where Feyd-Rautha fights a captive gladiator on his birthday. Position estimated.
Feyd-Rautha fights a captured Atreides soldier here. The man is meant to be drugged but is not; Feyd wins with a hidden trick and is cheered by the crowd.
Where the Baron watches the fight, with Count Fenring and Lady Margot as his guests.
The Bene Gesserit fortress where Miles Teg trains the boy ghola Duncan Idaho and Lucilla waits to imprint him. Position estimated.
The fortress defences. Killers break in to murder the ghola, and Teg and Lucilla slip out with him into the wild country.
Where the old Bashar teaches the boy Duncan to fight, while Lucilla watches and the Keep’s commander Schwangyu schemes against Taraza’s plan.
The Baron’s fortress, where he and Piter de Vries plan the trap for House Atreides. Position estimated.
Where the Baron, buoyed on suspensors, lays out the plan against House Atreides with his Mentat Piter de Vries and his nephew Feyd-Rautha.
The heir’s quarters. After Feyd’s plot against his uncle fails, the Baron makes him kill every woman of his pleasure wing.
An ancient Harkonnen hiding place, invisible to prescience, where Teg restores Duncan’s original memories. Position estimated.
A Harkonnen shelter hidden from prescient sight. Teg hides Lucilla and Duncan here and wakes the boy’s memories of his first life before Lucilla can imprint him.
Gammu’s great city, once the Harkonnen capital Barony. Teg gathers old veterans in its bars here, and Murbella first meets Duncan here. Position estimated.
Where Teg finds the old soldiers who fought under him and gathers them for his escape.
The great city of Gammu, grown out of the Harkonnen capital. The Honored Matres hold it in force.
A marker for the makers’ world itself: the novels show what comes out of Ix far more than the planet. Position estimated.
Source of the Ixian devices of the later books: the envoy Hwi Noree, made to be Leto II’s perfect match, the navigation machines that threaten the Guild, and the no-ships hidden from prescience.
The Great Honored Matre’s stronghold on the old Guild world. Position estimated.
Where Teg’s forces strike when the Sisterhood attacks Junction.
Where Dama rules until her adviser Logno takes her place, and where Murbella kills Logno and is hailed by the Honored Matres.
Shaddam IV’s court, where Irulan grows up. Position estimated.
The court where Princess Irulan grows up, and where the Reverend Mother Mohiam serves her father as Truthsayer.
The throne of the Padishah Emperors. From his court Shaddam IV lends his Sardaukar to the Harkonnens, and later sets out with them for Arrakis.
The Sisterhood’s centre of learning, burned by the Honored Matres. Position estimated.
A great Bene Gesserit school, destroyed with its Reverend Mothers. Only Lucilla escapes, carrying their shared memories.
The farm where the old Bashar lives in retirement. Position estimated.
Teg’s home among his fields, where Taraza’s summons finds him and calls him back to service.
Where the Fremen legions fought for Naraj. Position estimated.
The defenders used a stone burner here, and the old Fedaykin Farok’s son was among those it blinded.
Farad’n’s household, where the plot against the Atreides twins is hatched. Position estimated.
The exiled Corrinos’ court. Jessica is brought here and teaches Farad’n the Bene Gesserit way, and he breaks with his mother.
Where Wensicia’s people train the Laza tigers sent to kill the Atreides twins.
The Emperor’s prison camps, where the survivors become Sardaukar. Position estimated.
A world so harsh that only the toughest prisoners live; from them the Emperor draws his Sardaukar.
The city of the Tleilaxu Masters, closed to outsiders. Position estimated.
The Masters’ secret council, sealed against spies. Tylwyth Waff and the others meet here to lay their plans against the Bene Gesserit and the returning Scattering.
Where the Tleilaxu grow their gholas and Face Dancers, the most jealously kept secret of their race.
The Bene Gesserit school that trains the Sisterhood’s acolytes. Position estimated.
Where acolytes are trained in the Sisterhood’s disciplines. Jessica learned her arts here under Mohiam.

In Dune Messiah the Reverend Mother Mohiam, the Steersman Edric, the Face Dancer Scytale and Princess Irulan meet on Wallach IX to plot against Paul, the navigator’s presence hiding them from his sight.

The one inhabited island. Fallom plays the islanders’ music, and Hiroko warns the visitors to run.
The islanders welcome the visitors warmly. Hiroko, a young woman who fishes and farms, takes to Trevize.
At night Hiroko tells Trevize the truth: the visitors carry an infection the islanders are immune to, to be set off when the fishing fleet returns. They leave before dawn.
Fallom picks up an islander’s flute and plays it by transducing power rather than breath. The islanders are enchanted.
Hardin attends Lepold’s coming of age here while Wienis launches the attack, and the Foundation’s priests turn Anacreon against its regent.
Lepold is crowned here at midnight, glowing with the aura the priests give him and seated on a floating throne. When the priests strike, the lights die, his aura goes dark and the throne drops.
Young King Lepold comes back from a hunt proud of his forty-sixth nyakbird, and his uncle talks him into war with the Foundation.

Wienis tells Hardin the fleet has sailed and calls him a prisoner of war. Here he watches his son read the priests’ ultimatum, orders his guards to shoot Hardin, and when they refuse fires himself, in vain.
When the power fails, Poly Verisof, the Foundation’s ambassador and high priest, leads a crowd outside, and Wienis orders the guards to fire on them.
A temple of the Foundation’s religion of science, whose priests run the atomic plants Anacreon depends on.
Foundation-trained priests tend the atomic machines here as holy mysteries. On Hardin’s word they go on strike, and Anacreon’s power stops.
Where Ponyets bargains for the condemned agent Eskel Gorov, around 135 F.E.
The Grand Master hears Ponyets out. The Elders’ religion forbids the Foundation’s gadgets, but gold might buy the prisoner’s life.

Ponyets arrives with a crude transmuter of his own making that turns iron into gold. He sells it to the ambitious councillor Pherl, and a recording of Pherl using forbidden technology makes him Ponyets’s partner.
Eskel Gorov, a Master Trader and Foundation agent, waits here under sentence of death for selling atomic goods.
Overgrown buildings where feral dogs attack the travellers, until Bliss turns them with fear.
Twenty thousand years of neglect have brought the Spacer city down. The travellers search the ruins and find nothing that tells them where Earth is.
A pack of wild dogs, descended from the Aurorans’ pets, closes in. Trevize’s weapon only enrages them, until Bliss magnifies their fear and they flee.

Mitza Lizalor, the minister in charge of transport, means to keep the Far Star for Comporellon. Trevize talks, and charms, his way to the ship’s release.
The Far Star is held here while Comporellon’s officials look for a way to take the advanced ship for themselves.
Vasil Deniador, a sceptical historian, tells them what Comporellon remembers of Earth and the first settlers.

head_text: The world-city — Gaal lands on Trantor and rides up an observation tower to see it: metal to every horizon. A stranger who chats with him there is an Imperial agent.
Seldon’s numbers — Seldon is waiting in Gaal’s hotel room. He shows him psychohistory at work on Trantor’s future, and the odds of its destruction are high. Soon afterwards Gaal is arrested.

head_text: Seldon on trial — The Commission of Public Safety tries Seldon. He predicts Trantor’s ruin and thirty thousand years of chaos, which his plan could cut to one thousand. He accepts the encyclopedia project’s exile to Terminus, a result he had planned.
Exile, not martyrdom — Linge Chen sees Seldon and Gaal in private. Rather than make a martyr, the Commission will send the Encyclopedia project to the remote world of Terminus, and Seldon accepts.
Two Foundations — In his office Seldon tells Gaal that the exile was what he wanted, and that a second Foundation will be set up at the other end of the Galaxy, at Star’s End.
The Encyclopedia Foundation — About 100,000 scientists settle the empty world of Terminus to write the Encyclopedia Galactica. Seldon dies on Trantor in 1 F.E.
Anacreon’s envoy — In 50 F.E. Hardin shows Anacreon’s envoy, Anselm haut Rodric, round the Encyclopedia Building with every courtesy. Afterwards Rodric demands a military base on Terminus.
Lord Dorwin’s empty promises — In 50 F.E. Anacreon demands bases on Terminus. An Imperial envoy visits; Salvor Hardin’s analysis shows his reassurances contain nothing at all.
A plant fails — News comes of an atomic disaster at Gamma Andromeda: the Empire can no longer keep its own machines running.

The first Seldon crisis — Hardin and Yohan Lee take power from the Encyclopedists. The Vault opens and Seldon reveals the Encyclopedia was a cover. Hardin sets the other kingdoms against Anacreon and Terminus stays free.

The Action Party — Thirty years on, Councilman Sef Sermak’s Action Party wants Terminus to arm and strike first, and calls Hardin a traitor for propping up the kingdoms. Its move to impeach him fails by a narrow vote.
A regent’s war — Young King Lepold comes back from the hunt, and his uncle, Prince Regent Wienis, talks him into war as soon as an old Imperial cruiser, refitted by the Foundation, is ready.

The second Seldon crisis — In 80 F.E. Prince Regent Wienis attacks with a refitted Imperial cruiser while Hardin visits. Its crew and Anacreon’s people obey the Foundation’s priests instead, and Wienis dies by his own blaster.
The lights go out — At midnight on Lepold’s coronation the priests strike. The ballroom goes dark, the king loses his glow, and outside Poly Verisof’s crowd faces Wienis’s guards.

Mutiny on the Wienis — Aboard the cruiser, named for the regent, the high priest Theo Aporat declares the ship cursed. When its systems die the crew seizes the regent’s son, Admiral Prince Lefkin, and makes him read the priests’ ultimatum over the hyperwave.
Seldon’s second visit — On the Foundation’s eightieth anniversary a packed Vault hears Seldon praise the outcome, and warn against turning the Foundation’s spiritual power into a weapon.
The transmuter — Around 135 F.E. the trader Limmar Ponyets frees a Foundation agent by trading a gold-making machine and blackmailing the man who used it.
A trader condemned — Around 135 F.E. Askone’s Elders sentence Master Trader Eskel Gorov to death for selling atomic goods. Limmar Ponyets is sent to get him out.
Gorov released — With Councillor Pherl now on his side, Ponyets gets Gorov released and a cargo of tin besides. Askone’s ban on Foundation technology begins to give way.
Mallow reaches Korell — Around 155 F.E. Hober Mallow comes to find three lost ships. He refuses sanctuary to a false missionary, and sells to the Commdor.
Selling to the Commdor — Mallow wins Commdor Asper Argo over with Foundation gadgets, and his wife with jewelled trinkets.
Imperial blasters — At a foundry Mallow notices that Korell’s guards carry atomic blasters marked with the Empire’s emblem. Someone is arming Korell.
The dying Empire — Mallow travels on to Siwenna and hears from Onum Barr how the Empire’s provinces are decaying, and that it is arming Korell.
A plant nobody understands — Mallow bribes his way into Siwenna’s atomic power plant and finds its tech-men keep it going without understanding it. The Empire is losing what it knows.
Mallow’s trial — Tried for murder over the missionary, Mallow proves he was a Korellian agent, and is elected mayor.
The third Seldon crisis — Korell declares war, but its industry runs on Foundation goods. When trade stops, Korell gives in without a battle: trade, not religion, now carries the Plan.
Bel Riose and Ducem Barr — Around 195 F.E. the young Imperial general Bel Riose seeks out Ducem Barr to learn about the magicians of the Periphery, then marches on the Foundation.
Riose recalled — Cleon II fears any successful general, and has Riose and his own secretary recalled and executed. A strong Empire cannot allow a strong subject: the crisis solves itself.
Siwenna rises — With Riose gone, Siwenna rebels and joins the Foundation. At the celebration Barr explains why the Empire could never have won.

Magnifico — Honeymooning on Kalgan, the Darells rescue a frightened clown who says he fled the Mule, the new warlord who took Kalgan without a fight. Captain Han Pritcher, a Foundation agent, joins them.
The Vault opens — Seldon’s image speaks of a civil war with the Traders, a crisis the Mule has made irrelevant. Seldon did not foresee him, and the Foundation falls without a fight.
Haven holds out — The Darells and the psychologist Ebling Mis flee to Haven, the last Trader world resisting. Its will collapses as the others did.
The last Emperor — They pass through Neotrantor, where Dagobert IX keeps a shadow court. The Emperor’s son tries to take Bayta, and is found dead.
Ebling Mis and the Library — In the ruins of the sacked capital, Mis works feverishly to find the Second Foundation, as if something drives him.
Bayta fires — As Mis is about to say where the Second Foundation is, Bayta shoots him. She has realised Magnifico is the Mule, who has been steering everyone toward the Second Foundation.
The Mule’s search — Five years into his reign the Mule sends Han Pritcher, his convert, and Bail Channis, an unconverted man, to look for the Second Foundation.
Star’s End — Channis leads them to Rossem, under Tazenda, claiming that Tazenda is the Star’s End of Seldon’s riddle.
Expected — The Tazendian governor receives them as if he knew they were coming. Pritcher begins to wonder why Channis finds his way so easily.
The First Speaker — The First Speaker appears: it was a trap, and Channis’s memories were false. The Mule’s mind is changed, and he returns to Kalgan to rule in peace until his death.
The conspirators — Around 376 F.E. Dr. Toran Darell and his friends fear the Second Foundation is steering them. His fourteen-year-old daughter Arkady listens in.
A stowaway — The circle sends the librarian Homir Munn to Kalgan to look for clues in the Mule’s palace. Arkady hides aboard his ship.
Arkady on Kalgan — Arkady stows away with Homir Munn to Kalgan. Lord Stettin wants her, and she escapes with help from his mistress Lady Callia.
The Mule’s palace opened — Through Lady Callia, Arkady gets Munn permission to search the records in the Mule’s palace. Stettin, meanwhile, decides the Plan no longer binds him.
Escape with the Palvers — Fleeing Stettin’s police, Arkady falls in with Preem Palver and his wife, a Trantorian trading couple, who take her with them.
The Palvers — The farmer Preem Palver and his wife hide Arkady and take her home to Trantor, as Stettin goes to war with the Foundation.
A message carried — Arkady talks Palver into a food run to Terminus, and he carries her message to her father.

A circle has no end — Arkady sends word that the Second Foundation is at the other end of the Galaxy, which, on a circle, is Terminus. Dr. Darell’s mind-static unmasks Pelleas Anthor, and then a nest of Second Foundationers on Terminus.
Arkady tested — Afraid his daughter’s mind was tampered with, Dr. Darell tests her, and finds nothing. Relieved, he believes the Second Foundation is gone.
The real Star’s End — The captured Second Foundationers were sacrifices. The Second Foundation is on Trantor, where all roads end, and its First Speaker is Preem Palver.

A crisis resolved — In 498 F.E. Seldon appears again in the Time Vault and Mayor Harla Branno is vindicated. Councilman Golan Trevize says the Plan works too well: the Second Foundation must still exist.
Trevize speaks out — Trevize tells the Council that the Plan is too perfect to be anything but steered by a hidden Second Foundation, and is arrested for treason.
Exiled with a scholar — Branno arrests Trevize and sends him off in the Far Star with the historian Janov Pelorat, who wants to find Earth, as bait for the Second Foundation.
The Far Star — Trevize and Pelorat leave Terminus in a new gravitic ship. Trevize decides to make for the Sayshell Sector rather than Trantor.

Gendibal and the anti-Mules — On Trantor Speaker Stor Gendibal finds a Hamish woman, Sura Novi, whose mind has been touched by someone more skilled than any Speaker. He sets out after Trevize, with Novi.
On the farm road — Outside the university grounds the Hamish farmer Karoll Rufirant picks a fight with Speaker Stor Gendibal, until a Hamish woman, Sura Novi, intervenes.
Delarmi’s challenge — Speaker Delora Delarmi moves to impeach Gendibal over the brawl. He answers with Novi’s mind, touched by a hand finer than any Speaker’s.
Sayshell — Trevize and Pelorat land on Sayshell, meet Munn Li Compor and learn from the historian Quintesetz of Gaia, a world the Sayshellians fear.
Compor’s warning — In Sayshell City Trevize’s old classmate Munn Li Compor finds them and passes on the legend that Earth is radioactive.
Gaia — Gaia captures the Far Star. Trevize and Pelorat meet Bliss and Dom and learn what Gaia is.
Drawn down — Near Gaia the Far Star stops answering its controls and is brought down to the surface.
The search for Earth — In 499 F.E. Trevize, Pelorat and Bliss leave Gaia in the Far Star to find Earth and test the choice.
Comporellon — Comporellon tries to take their ship. Trevize charms Minister Lizalor, and Deniador gives them the positions of three forbidden worlds.
Held at Comporellon — Comporellon’s officials detain the travellers and keep the Far Star, hoping to take the advanced ship for themselves.
Three forbidden worlds — The historian Vasil Deniador shares Comporellon’s old tales and the positions of three Spacer worlds said to lie near Earth.
Aurora’s dogs — The first Spacer world is empty, and its dogs have gone wild.
Solaria and Fallom — Sarton Bander intends to kill them. Bliss acts and he dies; they rescue his child Fallom, who would otherwise be destroyed.
A Solarian host — Robots meet the Far Star, and Sarton Bander, the estate’s only human, shows the visitors round with pride, explaining how Solarians power their robots with their own brains.
Fallom taken aboard — Bliss insists they take Bander’s young child with them, and they escape the estate with Fallom before more Solarians can act.
Fifty worlds — On an airless world they find the list of all fifty Spacer worlds. Plotted in space, they point to the centre, and to Earth.
The moss — Back outside, they find moss growing round their suit seals, feeding on their breath. They destroy it so that nothing is carried off the planet.
New Earth — The friendly islanders of Alpha plan to kill them with a disease. Hiroko warns them away.
A warm welcome — The islanders of Alpha greet the travellers with food, music and friendship, and Hiroko takes to Trevize.
Fallom’s flute — Fallom plays an islander’s flute without breathing into it, drawing the sound out by transducing power. The islanders are enchanted.
Earth found — Earth is radioactive and dead. But its moon is very large.
Into the Moon — An opening appears in the lunar surface and the Far Star is drawn into a hidden hangar.
Daneel — Under the Moon waits R. Daneel Olivaw, who has watched humanity for twenty thousand years and set up Gaia and psychohistory. He is dying, and Fallom is his answer.
Galaxia confirmed — Trevize understands why he chose Gaia: a united Galaxy could face whatever might come from outside it. Then he looks at Fallom, uneasy.
An audience with Cleon I — The Emperor wants predictions he can use. Seldon says the theory is not practical, and is let go.
Hummin and Dors — A journalist, Chetter Hummin, warns that First Minister Demerzel is hunting him, and hides him at Streeling University with Dors Venabili.
In the library — Seldon reads history at Streeling, looking for a smaller, simpler society to test psychohistory on, and grows fascinated by hints of a single first world of humanity.
Up to the roof — Seldon talks his way onto the meteorologist Jenarr Leggen’s next trip to Upperside.
Lost Upperside — Seldon wanders off on the domes, hides from a prowling jet-down, loses his way and nearly dies of cold.
Dors searches — Dors forces a search. With the help of Leggen and the seismologist Rogen Benastra she finds Seldon, half-frozen.
Mycogen — On a tour of the microfarms, Sister Raindrop Forty-Three lends Seldon the sector’s sacred Book, which outsiders are never meant to read.
Guests of Mycogen — Hummin moves them to Mycogen, where Sunmaster Fourteen, head of its Elders, accepts them grudgingly as guests, in kirtles and with their hair hidden.
The Book — Most of the Book disappoints him, but two things do not: the name of the Mycogenians’ lost world, Aurora, and its robots.
The Sacratorium — Seldon and Dors break into Mycogen’s temple seeking a robot and are caught. Hummin gets them out.
The gravibus — Disguised as a Mycogenian, Seldon rides toward the Sacratorium and falls into talk with an old scholar, Mycelium Seventy-Two.
The robot in the Aerie — Seldon climbs into the Elders’ Aerie and finds the robot: a metal figure in human form, motionless, kept as a relic.
The heat sinks — In Dahl they meet Yugo Amaryl, a heat-sinker with a gift for mathematics.
Lodgers in Dahl — In Dahl Seldon and Dors rent rooms from Jirad Tisalver and his family.
Raych and Mother Rittah — In Billibotton a street boy, Raych, guides them, and an old woman tells Seldon of Earth and of Aurora, Earth’s enemy.
Dors draws her knives — Toughs corner the visitors in Billibotton. Dors fights their leader with two knives, beats him, and becomes a legend in the slum.
Davan — The agitator Davan asks for Seldon’s help in uniting Trantor’s downtrodden against the Empire. Seldon decides that psychohistory will help them more.
Betrayed — Mrs. Tisalver informs on her lodgers, and Raych leads Seldon and Dors away through the sewers beneath Dahl.
Rashelle’s coup — Wye kidnaps Seldon to lend Rashelle’s coup the weight of psychohistory. Demerzel’s forces end it.
Taken to Wye — Sergeant Emmer Thalus brings Seldon, Dors and Raych to Wye. Its ruler, Rashelle, wants Seldon’s science to bless her bid for the throne, and Seldon refuses.
Joranum — In 12,028 G.E. the populist Laskin Joranum threatens Demerzel. Seldon unmasks Joranum’s past instead; Demerzel retires and Seldon becomes First Minister.
The gardener — Attacked on the Palace grounds, Seldon is defended by Dors and by a gardener, Mandell Gruber, who becomes his friend.
Namarti’s long game — From Wye, Joranum’s old lieutenant Namarti rebuilds the movement and spends years arranging small breakdowns in Trantor’s services, to turn people against their rulers.
Raych undercover — Raych goes undercover among the conspirators. They drug him so that he will kill his own father at a Palace ceremony.
The Emperor killed — Around 12,038 G.E. a plot through Wye and a drugged Raych is foiled by Manella Dubanqua, but in the confusion a gardener kills Cleon I. A military junta takes over.
Raych falls — Raych dies on Santanni during its revolt. The ship carrying Manella and Bellis away is lost.
Yugo’s death — Yugo Amaryl, Seldon’s first partner in psychohistory, dies, worn out by the work.
Wanda and the mentalics — Seldon’s granddaughter Wanda can read minds. With her and Stettin Palver he gathers mentalics, the hidden Second Foundation, inside the Galactic Library.
An encyclopedia — Seldon wins the Chief Librarian, Las Zenow, over to an encyclopedia project, and the Library opens its resources to the work.

Terminus chosen — The Library’s search of old records turns up a remote, empty world at the edge of the Galaxy. The Encyclopedia project gives Seldon his public Foundation there, while the Commission rules behind a powerless Emperor.
Seldon’s death — In 12,069 G.E. (1 F.E.) Seldon dies at his desk, both Foundations set in motion.
The old Gaian Dom explains Gaia to Pelorat and Trevize. Bliss is the part of Gaia who meets them.
Mild weather and quiet: everything here shares one mind. Pelorat is delighted; Trevize is wary.
A plain house in gentle country. Old Dom, whose full name runs to many syllables, explains that he, the house and the land around it are all Gaia.
Where Gaia brings the Far Star down.
Gaia takes control of the Far Star in space and brings it down here, its controls no longer answering Trevize.
The atomic plant whose failure kills a great many people, news of which reaches Terminus around 50 F.E.
Poor maintenance lets the plant fail, with terrible loss of life. To Hardin it is proof that the Empire can no longer run its own machines.
Haven’s cities lie under the rock. Here Toran’s family plots the Traders’ resistance.
Haven’s people live in cities carved under its barren surface. The Darells and Ebling Mis shelter here when the Foundation falls, and watch the last Traders lose heart.
Kalgan’s link to the stars, and Arkady’s way off the planet.
Running from Stettin’s police, Arkady falls in with Preem Palver and his wife, who take her with them to Trantor.
The seat of Kalgan’s warlords, and then of the Mule.
The seat of Kalgan’s warlords. The Mule takes it without a fight and rules his Union of Worlds from here.
After the Mule’s death his palace is kept as it was. Homir Munn comes to Kalgan hoping to search the records there for clues to the Second Foundation.
Where Stettin, who has taken the Mule’s title of First Citizen, decides the Plan is nonsense and plans war, and where his mistress Lady Callia takes a liking to Arkady.
Beaches and carnivals where the Darells find Magnifico running from the Mule’s men.
Kalgan’s pleasure grounds, built for Imperial nobles at play. Bayta and Toran honeymoon here and save a terrified clown, Magnifico, from the Mule’s soldiers.
Mallow sells Asper Argo trinkets for his wife here, and in Korell’s foundries he notices the Empire’s spaceship-and-sun on the guards’ weapons.
Korell’s industry; its layout here is schematic.
Mallow shows the Commdor his wares here, jewelled trinkets for the Commdora among them, and wins her over.
Seat of Commdor Asper Argo. Years after Mallow’s visit, Argo debates war with the Foundation here, and his wife cannot bear to lose her Foundation gadgets.
A man calling himself a Foundation missionary begs Mallow for sanctuary. Mallow hands him over to the crowd, suspecting a trap; he is right.
Mallow’s trading ship waits at a remote field for an audience. A hurt man calling himself the Reverend Jord Parma gets aboard, and Mallow hands him to the Korellians outside.
A wall plaque of the fifty Spacer worlds. Plotted, they form a sphere, and Earth should lie near its centre.
Trevize and Pelorat walk in spacesuits into an airless library and find a plaque giving the names and positions of all fifty Spacer worlds.
A hungry moss, all that lives here, gathers round the seals of their suits to feed on the traces of breath leaking out. They burn it off before leaving.
A hidden hangar and halls under the lunar crust, where the last answers of the series are given.
R. Daneel Olivaw tells them his story: twenty thousand years guarding humanity, Gaia and psychohistory among his works. His brain is failing, and he wants to merge it with Fallom’s.
An entrance opens in the Moon’s surface and the Far Star is drawn inside.
A country palace standing in for the lost splendour of Trantor.
Neotrantor is a farm world, and the palace sits among its fields. The travellers come down here on their way to Trantor.
The last Emperor keeps his shadow court here, ruling a handful of farm worlds as if they were still the Galaxy.
Where the Tazendian governor receives Channis and Pritcher, and the Mule confronts Channis.
Tazenda’s governor receives Channis and Pritcher, and seems an entirely ordinary man.
Pritcher arrests Channis here. The Mule arrives, breaks Channis, and is himself defeated when the First Speaker appears.
A poor, cold farming village. Its Elders make it plain that the Tazendian governor is already expecting the visitors.
Where Raych dies in the uprising.
Raych is killed here during Santanni’s revolt against the junta.
The capital. Trevize meets his old classmate Munn Li Compor here, and a guide shows them the city.
Compor turns up here and tells them the old story that Earth is radioactive, and that nobody can find it.
Pelorat consults the historian Quintesetz, who gives them Gaia’s coordinates and the local legends about it.
Professor Quintesetz knows Pelorat’s work. He tells them, reluctantly, where Gaia lies, and how Sayshell has come to fear it.
Home of the once-great patrician Barr family, now poor. Onum Barr tells Mallow how the Empire is rotting.
Bel Riose comes here to question Onum’s son Ducem about the Foundation. Barr shows him a small force-field device that a Foundation trader left with his father.
Onum Barr, a ruined old patrician living in a barren corner of the world, tells Mallow what the viceroys did to Siwenna and helps him with a passport.
Mallow bribes a tech-man with a personal shield to show him round. The men running it keep it going by rote and can no longer repair it; later the tech-man complains that his shield went dead.
A mansion among endless orchards and fields, kept by robots. Here Bander dies and Fallom is saved.
Fields and orchards worked entirely by robots, powered through Bander’s own transducer lobes. Bander shows them round with pride.
Robots meet the ship. Sarton Bander, the estate’s one human, receives the visitors, curious about people who come in the flesh.
Most of it lies underground. Bander turns on the visitors to kill them; Bliss turns the energy back and Bander dies.
Bander’s young child Fallom lives here with a robot nurse. With Bander dead, the Solarians would kill the child as surplus, so the travellers take Fallom with them.
Seat of the mayors of Terminus and their Council, from Salvor Hardin on.
Where the Council of Terminus sits. The Action Party’s move to impeach Hardin narrowly fails here, and Mallow’s trial is broadcast from here across Foundation space.
Hardin keeps a framed motto on his wall, that violence is the last refuge of the incompetent. Every later mayor governs from here.
Where Dr. Toran Darell’s circle meets to hunt the Second Foundation, and his daughter Arkady listens in.
With Dr. Semic, Darell builds a device that fills the air with mental static, unbearable to anyone with mind powers. It unmasks Anthor, and later Darell uses his instruments to test Arkady.
The conspirators meet here. Pelleas Anthor shows them brain recordings of leading men with the same odd flattening, which he calls the Tamper Plateau, and Arkady eavesdrops from her room.
The capital, on the only large island. Salvor Hardin is its first mayor, and the city outgrows the Encyclopedia to rule the Periphery.
Where Sef Sermak and the young councilmen of the Action Party plot to replace Hardin, convinced that his religion of science is betraying the Foundation.
Home of the Encyclopedia Foundation and its Board of Trustees under Lewis Pirenne, whose scholars spend fifty years preparing the first volume. Hardin shows Anacreon’s envoy round it.
The rich Master Trader’s home. Mallow plans his run for office here with Ankor Jael, and Jorane Sutt comes to bargain with him.
Terminus’s link to the rest of the Galaxy. Arkady Darell slips aboard Homir Munn’s ship here to follow him to Kalgan.
A sealed room Seldon left behind. At each crisis it opens and his recorded image speaks to whoever is there.
A glass enclosure at the front of the Vault. At the appointed time the lights dim and Seldon’s image appears in it, an old man in a wheelchair, to speak to whoever has come.
Rows of seats facing the cubicle, where the Foundation’s leaders gather at each appointed time to hear what Seldon has to say.
Dahl’s notorious slum, where Seldon and Dors find the street boy Raych and the old woman Mother Rittah, who tells them legends of Earth.
The agitator Davan, who wants to unite Trantor’s downtrodden against the Empire, asks Seldon for help. Seldon decides psychohistory is the better help.
An old woman tells Seldon and Dors legends of Earth, the true first home, of Aurora, its enemy, and of robots from the oldest stories.
A crowd of Billibotton toughs led by Marron corners the visitors. Dors beats Marron with two knives and becomes a local legend.
The ruling commission that tries Seldon in 12,067 G.E. and sends his project into exile on Terminus.
Where Chief Commissioner Linge Chen and his colleagues see Seldon and Gaal in private, and offer exile to Terminus in place of a verdict that could make Seldon a martyr.

head_text: Gaal rides up to view Trantor and sees metal stretching to the horizon, with no greenery visible. Jerril talks with him and calls Seldon “Raven.”
The Imperial Library, the greatest store of knowledge in the Galaxy, and the one great building left standing after the Sack.
The great Imperial Library. When Trantor is sacked it is spared, and its records still reach back across the whole history of the Empire.
Where Ebling Mis buries himself in the old records, working without rest or food, while Bayta, Toran and Magnifico look after him.
Seldon’s encyclopedia work in the Library, and the cover under which Wanda Seldon and Stettin Palver quietly gather other mentalics: the start of a second Foundation inside the Library.
The office of Las Zenow, the Chief Librarian; its layout here is schematic.
A closed, bald-headed, religious sector that farms yeast and algae. Its people keep a Book about their lost home, Aurora, and a secret in their Sacratorium.
A gravitic bus runs toward the Sacratorium. On it Seldon falls into talk with an old scholar, Mycelium Seventy-Two.
Where Seldon and Dors live as tolerated outsiders, in kirtles and with their hair hidden, and where Seldon reads the Book and finds in it Aurora and robots.
Vats of yeast and algae below Mycogen, the source of foods prized by Trantor’s rich. On a tour Sister Raindrop Forty-Three shows Seldon round and, against the rules, lends him the Book.
The only open land on Trantor: parkland, gardens and the Palace in the Imperial Sector, where the Emperors hold court.

Grass, trees and paths under real sky, kept by a corps of gardeners. Cleon I walks and talks here with his First Ministers, and the gardener Mandell Gruber becomes Seldon’s friend after helping fight off an attacker.
Seat of the First Minister, the Emperor’s chief official, who runs the Empire day to day while the Emperor reigns.
The Emperor’s residence and court, at the heart of the one stretch of Trantor left open to the sky.
Mycogen’s temple, where Seldon and Dors break in looking for an ancient robot and are caught.
The Elders’ sanctum above the temple, closed to everyone else. Seldon climbs up into it.
Mycogen’s temple, a place of mourning for Aurora, the world its people believe was stolen from them. Old screens show Aurora’s landscapes.
Mycogen’s holiest relic: a motionless metal figure in human shape, kept in the Aerie. It is not the living robot Seldon hoped to question.
The university where Seldon’s project works, far from the trial chamber. After the verdict soldiers guard it while the project gets ready to leave.
After the trial Seldon tells Gaal the rest of the plan: there will be two Foundations, one on Terminus and the other at Star’s End.
The old university buildings where the Second Foundation meets around the Speakers’ Table, hidden behind the Hamish farm country.
Old buildings and walks where the Second Foundationers live apart. The Hamish farmers around them see only a community of scholars, and resent them.
The device that displays the Plan’s equations, which every Speaker studies and amends. Gendibal’s study of it convinces him that someone else is keeping the Plan on course.
The council of the Second Foundation: the First Speaker, Quindor Shandess, and the Speakers. Delora Delarmi moves to impeach Stor Gendibal here, and he answers by showing them Sura Novi’s mind.
The university in the Streeling Sector where Hummin hides Seldon and he meets the historian Dors Venabili.
Seldon reads history here, hunting for a society small and simple enough to model, and keeps finding how little is known of humanity’s first world.
Meteorologists ride up from here to work on top of the domes. Seldon gets himself included on one of Jenarr Leggen’s trips.
Where the old Seldon goes on working after almost everyone he loved is gone, and where he dies at his desk with the Prime Radiant in his hand.
The research group Seldon builds at Streeling over the decades, with Yugo Amaryl at his side, growing into a large staff of mathematicians working on the Prime Radiant.
The campus quarters Hummin arranges for Seldon, with the historian Dors Venabili asked to look after him.
The roof of the domes, under real weather. Seldon goes up with a meteorologist, is left behind in the cold, and is found half-frozen by Dors.
Cold and empty, under an open sky. Seldon wanders off alone, hides from a passing jet-down, and cannot find his way back.
Weather instruments on the dome roofs, where the meteorologist Jenarr Leggen and his team study Trantor’s real climate.
A powerful sector near the south pole, ruled by Mayor Mannix IV. His daughter Rashelle kidnaps Seldon to lend her coup legitimacy; Demerzel crushes it.
A guarded office in Wye from which Namarti runs what is left of Joranum’s movement, planning years of small breakdowns to turn Trantor against its rulers.
Seat of Wye’s mayors. Rashelle, who rules in place of her ageing father Mannix IV, keeps Seldon here as an honoured prisoner while Wye prepares to seize the throne.

head_text: Sent to the Chantry — His father means to send him to the Chantry’s seminary on Vesperad. Gibson is caught helping him and is maimed and exiled.
Flight from Delos — His mother arranges his escape. After a fight with his brother Crispin, he boards the Eurynasir at Karch, bound for Teukros.
Stranded on Emesh — He wakes years later robbed and abandoned on Emesh, far off course, and lives as a beggar in Borosevo. His friend Cat dies of plague.
Myrmidon — He fights in the Colosso as a gladiator, alongside Switch and Pallino.
Count Mataro’s house — The count takes Hadrian in as a companion for his daughter. He meets the Tavrosi xenologist Valka Onderra and kills the Chantry priest Gilliam Vas in a duel.
The ruins of Calagah — In the Quiet’s black ruins Hadrian has visions. A Cielcin ship of Clan Otiolo lands nearby.
Battle of Emesh — Imperial legions under Raine Smythe and a Jaddian knight, Olorin Milta, defeat the Cielcin. ISD 16172.

Uvanari — Hadrian interprets for the captured Cielcin captain, then grants it a merciful death in exchange for the location of Vorgossos. His father disowns him, and the Meidua Red Company is founded to find it.

head_text: The Consortium — House Marlowe does business with the Wong-Hopper Consortium.
Games in the Colosso — Hadrian watches the Colosso games with his family and is sickened by the killing his brother Crispin relishes.
Aboard the Eurynasir — Hadrian goes into fugue aboard the merchant ship for the long voyage to the scholiasts of Teukros.
The captive Cielcin — Captured Cielcin are held and questioned in Borosevo. Hadrian secretly goes to speak with their captain and is caught.
The Lesser Devil — Crispin and Sabine Marlowe crash in the Redtine Mountains and find a hidden village, in a novella set on Delos.
First contact — Three centuries before Hadrian is born, humans meet the Cielcin for the first time at Cressgard, ISD 15792. The colony is lost.
Cai Shen burns — While Hadrian is still a boy, the Cielcin burn the Mandari world of Cai Shen and its famous temple, ISD 16130.
Forty-eight years on — After half a century of fruitless searching, the Red Company is at Rustam. Hadrian kills the Extrasolarian called the Painted Man in Arslan.
March Station — The broker Antonius Brevon sells passage to Vorgossos for Tanaran’s blood. On the Sojourner Enigma of Hours, an oracle speaks Cat’s last words to him.
The Undying King — Hadrian meets Kharn Sagara, who has lived for millennia by moving his mind into cloned bodies.
Brethren — Under the ice lies Brethren, the last Mericanii machine mind, which shows Hadrian possible futures.
Tyras destroyed — Just before the story resumes, the Cielcin destroy the annexed freehold of Tyras, ISD 16216.
The wound at Rustam — A Cielcin attack has torn a fifty-mile rent in Rustam’s crust where its old capital stood. Refugees live in a city of grounded ships.
Switch sent away — Switch betrays a secret on Vorgossos, and Hadrian sends one of his oldest friends away.
The Emperor’s summons — A century on, Sir Hadrian commands the Tamerlane. After Hermonassa falls, William XXIII sends him with Prince Alexander to find two missing legions.
Fort Din — On Gododdin Hadrian forbids the decimation of mutinous Irchtani auxiliaries and wins their loyalty.
Battle of the Beast — A Cielcin gravity net pulls the fleet from warp. Hadrian boards the worldship and kills Iubalu of the White Hand. ISD 16534.
Triumph and treachery — Hadrian is given a triumph in the capital and betrothed to Princess Selene. Valka is wounded by an assassin.
Gibson and the Horizon — On Colchis Hadrian finds Gibson alive. A Mericanii ship mind hidden in Gabriel’s Archive gives him the way to the Quiet.
The Mountain — On Annica Hadrian climbs to the summit and meets the Quiet, who show him time and give him the power to choose between possible outcomes.
Battle of Berenike — The Cielcin destroy much of the Imperial fleet and Titus Hauptmann dies. Valka is cut down by the sorcerer Urbaine and put into fugue. ISD 16701.
The Demon in White — Hadrian walks out alone to surrender to Dorayaica. The worldship’s gun fires and misses, because he chooses the world in which it misses.
The duel with Irshan — His enemies at court force him into a duel in the flooded Grand Colosseum against the Jaddian gladiator Irshan.
Queen Amid Ashes — The Red Company’s first official mission defeats Prince Muzugara on Thagura, ISD 16257.
The Demons of Arae — The Red Company fights mercenaries on the salt flats of Arae, ISD 16443.
Hermonassa falls — The Cielcin prince Syriani Dorayaica routs the defenders of the Red Star Foundries shipyard.
Recalled to Eikana — Hadrian is brought out of exile to save the antimatter refinery from Hushansa of the White Hand. ISD 17006.
Exile on Nessus — At Maddalo House he and Valka have lived quietly for decades. The Emperor’s agents send him as envoy to the Lothrians.
The embassy — The Lothrian Conclave is already allied with Dorayaica and feeding its own people to the Cielcin. The Red Company fights its way across Vedatharad.
Taken — In the Grand Conclave the sorcerer Urbaine captures Hadrian and gives him to the Cielcin.
Seven years in the dark — Hadrian is imprisoned and tortured aboard the Dharan-Tun, and loses his hold on his power.
The Black Feast — At Akterumu Dorayaica sacrifices the Cielcin princes to the dead god Miudanar and is crowned. The Red Company is massacred and the Tamerlane brought down. ISD 17061.
The Isle of the Dead — After decades adrift, Hadrian and Valka hide on Colchis and honour their dead.
Trial for witchcraft — Between the books Hadrian spends twelve years on trial before the Chantry, then decades in internal exile.
Gibson’s secret — Gibson dies, and Hadrian learns his tutor was born a Bourbon prince.
Lorian found — Back on Nessus they find Lorian alive in fugue.
The Emperor in the field — At Carteia William XXIII meets Hadrian in secret and shows him what his service knows of extinct civilizations.
Battle of Ganelon — Hadrian destroys the MINOS laboratory making a plague. A Jaddian prince, Kaim-Olorin, proves to be Olorin Milta from Emesh. ISD 17131.
News from Perfugium — At Fidchell Station word comes that the Emperor is besieged.
Battle of Perfugium — Seven worldships fall on the Emperor’s tour. Hadrian, Lin and Kaim save William XXIII, but Valka dies in the evacuation. ISD 17136.
The blow — When the Emperor dismisses Valka’s death, Hadrian breaks his nose. He is condemned to the prison world Belusha and escapes with Lorian’s help.
Refuge on Jadd — Hadrian reaches Jadd with Prince Kaim-Olorin, carrying what is left of Valka.
The Enar homeworld — An Enar tablet captured from the Cielcin points to Vaiartu, the homeworld of the Firstborn, the farthest east of the mapped worlds.
Two hundred years on Jadd — Hadrian has raised a daughter, Cassandra, from Valka’s genetic material. She passes the Fire School’s Trial of the Heart.
A Watcher wakes — Summoned by the Emperor’s service, Hadrian finds the Watcher Ushara under the Enar ruins. Cielcin attack, and orbital fire shatters the god. ISD 17410.
Murdered by the Chantry — At court Hadrian meets Crown Prince Aurelian. The Chantry dissolves him with poison.
The City at the End of Time — A trillion years ahead, the Judicator Ragama resurrects Hadrian and burns away the Watcher’s influence.
The Monarch — On Lorian’s ship Hadrian reaches Latarra. Its Monarch is another Kharn Sagara, and becomes an ally.
Battle of Vorgossos — Imperial, Latarran and Chantry fleets take Vorgossos. Hadrian kills Kharn’s heirs, drowns Brethren, spares the new machine Orphan, and takes the Demiurge. ISD 17458.
Nessus falls — In the years before the book opens, the Cielcin take Nessus, the seat of the Magnarch of Centaurus where Hadrian once lived in exile.
Monmara destroyed — The Norman water world where the Red Company was formally founded has been destroyed by the Cielcin.
The Fangs of Oannos — A story set in the Kingdom of the Three Suns during Hadrian’s years on Jadd.
Through Tiryns — From Sabratha Hadrian travels by way of Tiryns, the Persean capital, on the road to Forum.
The Dregs of Empire — Lorian Aristedes, sent to Belusha in Hadrian’s place, survives the prison world.
Exile on Annica — A fugitive from Empire and Chantry, Hadrian waits beyond the core with Cassandra.
The muster at Tenba — The last fleets of humanity gather.
Catraeth burns — An explosion devastates Catraeth, and Hadrian is blamed.
The Sun Eater — Miudanar rises over Ywain. Hadrian drives Gododdin’s star to hypernova, destroying the Cielcin host, the Watchers, and the system with billions of people in it.
After — The Cielcin are broken and Alexander takes the throne. The old man in the Library finishes his account.
The capital has fallen — Hadrian learns that the Eternal City has fallen to the Cielcin, and that the Chantry hid the news for nearly two years.
The host comes to Gododdin — Humanity masters its last fleets at Gododdin. The Cielcin come with their worldships and the Watchers.
