The way back to the physical world shown on Starling’s old map.
A tunnel that may be a way past the Dakwara.
A giant serpent that guards the central island.
Starling’s cargo starship and its crew of misfits from many worlds.
A ring-shaped island around a lake of not-water, guarded by Scadrian warships. The crew believes the small central island holds the hidden perpendicularity.
Raoden is taken — The prince of Arelon wakes with the Shaod and is quietly thrown into Elantris, declared dead to the world.
The Well of Ascension — Vin reaches the Well and gives up its power, freeing the thing that had been tricking her.
The Rift burns — In Dalinar’s returning memories, the Blackthorn burns the rebel city, not knowing his wife Evi is inside.
Azir joins — Lift unlocks Azimir’s Oathgate and Dalinar wins the Azish to his coalition, before talks with the singers collapse.
The Cult of Moments — Shallan seeks to infiltrate the Cult of Moments in Kholinar.
The Wall Guard — Kaladin fights beside Highmarshal Azure’s guard on the walls until a thunderclast breaks through.
Vision at the lighthouse — Kaladin looks into a heatless fire and sees Thaylen City overrun and Dalinar surrounded.
The Bondsmith mends — Dalinar finds he can mend what is broken, and Queen Fen joins his coalition.
The Eila Stele — A translated stone says humans came to Roshar as the invaders, and the coalition starts to come apart.
The King’s Drop — A thunderclast smashes the Gemstone Reserve. Dalinar traps the Unmade Nergaoul in the great gem, and the possessed soldiers come back to themselves.
Excommunicated — On a visit to Vedenar, the Vorin church casts Dalinar out.
Hearthstone — Navani’s flying platform lifts the townsfolk out while Kaladin duels the Fused Leshwi. At the manor, Moash kills Roshone.
Fadrex and the caches — Searching for the Lord Ruler’s storehouses, the crew lays siege to Fadrex as the world falls apart.
The surgeon’s son — Relieved of command, Kaladin works with his father among the tower’s wounded in mind.
A new Bondsmith — Navani bonds the Sibling, and together they drive the corruption out of the tower.
The dragon’s bargain — On the Crimson Sea Tress bargains with the dragon Xisis, and Captain Crow ends up in the dragon’s service.
The yoki-hijo — Yumi spends her days in ritual, stacking stones to call the spirits that warm her people’s land.
The painters’ stand — Nikaro gathers painters at the edge of the shroud against an army of nightmares, and paints them back into people.
The Refuge — Scadrian scientists hidden under the surface refuse to help Beacon and keep from Nomad the Dor he needs to leave.
The Cinder King falls — Nomad faces the Cinder King on Union’s deck, drains his power and Skips away as the sunlight takes him.
Into the Spiritual Realm — Dalinar opens a perpendicularity in the tower and goes with Navani into the Spiritual Realm to learn the truth about the past.
Taln’s Honorblade — At Stoneward Szeth kills a corrupted stone shaman and takes back the first of the stolen Honorblades.
The Hero of Ages — Sazed takes up both Shards and restores the world, clearing the ash.
Kaladin and Nale — Kaladin duels the Herald Nale, who yields his Honorblade and reveals what Ishar has done to Shinovar.
The Fifth Ideal — Ishar raises corrupted Honorbearers against them. Kaladin speaks the Fifth Ideal and frees Ishar, and Szeth fights with Nightblood.
The defence of Azimir — Adolin helps the Azish defend the Oathgate under the Grand Market dome against Odium’s armies and a thunderclast, at terrible cost to himself.
Bridge Four on Narak — Sigzil and Bridge Four hold four fortresses on Narak. They fall one by one, and Venli’s chasmfiends storm Narak Prime.
Fen’s choice — Odium out-argues Jasnah over the contest’s terms, and Queen Fen signs Thaylenah over to him without a battle.
Cusicesh speaks — For the first time, the great spirit of Kasitor speaks to the Iriali and opens a gateway for them to leave Roshar.
December of Rivershore — An orphan raised at a riverside inn sees the river curdle and a plague take her town.
Warning the king — December warns King Beaudilog’s court of the plague and of the demon; the king’s ministers dismiss her.
The Megalith wakes — The city’s guards turn on each other, and plotters release the Megalith through the palace’s river of demon blood.
Siri’s marriage — Siri of Idris arrives at the Court of Gods to marry the God King of Hallandren.
Lightsong’s last day — In captivity, Lightsong gives his Breath to heal Susebron, sacrificing himself to restore the God King’s tongue.
Vasher and Nightblood — Vasher and Nightblood work to prevent a new war between Hallandren and Idris; Vasher’s past is tied to the earlier Manywar.
The assassin in white — Szeth kills King Gavilar in Kholinar on the night of the treaty feast.
Bridge Four — Kaladin, a surgeon’s son turned soldier turned slave, carries bridges in the plateau runs and keeps his crew alive.
Jasnah’s ward — Shallan Davar talks her way into Jasnah Kholin’s service, planning to steal her Soulcaster.
A widow before the wedding — Sarene reaches Kae and learns that Raoden is reported dead; their contract makes her his widow.
Battle of the Tower — Abandoned by Sadeas, Dalinar’s army is saved when Kaladin leads his bridgemen back.
The visions — In the storms Dalinar sees the past and hears a voice that admits it is dying.
To the centre of the Plains — Dalinar marches on the Parshendi city as they summon a new storm from the west.
Urithiru found — Shallan opens the Oathgate and leads the armies to the lost tower city.
Kaladin’s Third Ideal — At the king’s palace in the warcamps, Kaladin speaks his Third Ideal while protecting Elhokar.
Damnation named — The Heralds’ torment between Desolations is laid bare, and the Everstorm brings the return of something long imprisoned.
Home from the Roughs — Waxillium Ladrian returns to Elendel to run his house, and is pulled back into lawkeeping by a run of train heists.
Shadows of Self — A rogue kandra murders her way through the city’s elite, and Harmony’s quiet influence comes into the open.
The Bands of Mourning — Wax’s crew chases a legendary relic and finds proof of other peoples beyond the sea.
The Emperor’s Soul — A condemned Forger is given a hundred days to rebuild the soul of a dying emperor.
Shadows for Silence — Silence goes after a dangerous bounty in the Forests of Hell with her daughter.
Edgedancer — Lift travels to Yeddaw in Tashikk, where Darkness has been reported.
A coalition — Dalinar tries to unite the monarchs of Roshar against the Voidbringers, with his own past catching up with him.
The fall of Kholinar — Kaladin, Shallan, Adolin and Elhokar slip into the occupied capital. The city falls and the king dies.
Across Shadesmar — Pulled through the Oathgate into the Cognitive Realm, the survivors walk and sail toward Thaylen City.
The land is part of the writing — Raoden discovers that adding a line for the Chasm lets his Aons function again.
The Battle of Thaylen Field — Odium sends his champion. Dalinar refuses to give in, binds the realms together and becomes the Bondsmith.
Dawnshard — Rysn’s ship sails for forbidden Akinah and finds something far older than the Radiants.
The tower occupied — The Fused take Urithiru. Navani, a prisoner, works out the science of Light.
Adolin’s trial — Adolin asks the honorspren to judge humanity, and stands up for the dead spren of his sword.
The Set in Bilming — Wax finally confronts the secret society behind years of crimes, and its link to a power from off the world.
Tress sets sail — When the duke’s son is sent off to the Sorceress, Tress leaves her island to get him back.
Elantris shines again — Raoden adds the missing Chasm line to the city-scale Aon, restoring Elantris.
The Sorceress’s island — With a pirate crew and an unusual narrator, Tress reaches the Midnight Sea and forces the Sorceress to leave the world.
Yumi and Nikaro — A stone-stacker and a nightmare painter are bound together across time and must work out why.
The shroud lifts — They destroy the machine behind the shroud, and the sun shines on Komashi again.
Nomad lands — Hunted by the Night Brigade, Nomad arrives on Canticle and is taken prisoner in Union.
Beacon stands — Nomad joins Beacon’s rebellion against the Cinder King, racing the sunrise.
Kaladin and Szeth in Shinovar — They cross the storms to Szeth’s homeland and find the Herald Ishar behind its silence.
Stormfall — Retribution’s ascension ends the old storms and leaves Roshar isolated in slowed time.

Jasnah in the alley — Jasnah lets thugs follow her into a dark alley and destroys them with her Soulcaster while Shallan watches.
Spears in the chasms — Sent down to scavenge the dead, Kaladin secretly teaches Bridge Four to fight with spears.
Szeth’s true master — The gentle King Taravangian reveals that he holds Szeth’s oathstone, and sends him to kill Dalinar.

Four against one — Adolin duels for Shardblades to help his father, until a match becomes four Shardbearers against him and Kaladin jumps into the ring.

Re-Shephir — Shallan tracks the killings to an Unmade hiding in the tower and drives it off with her Lightweaving.
Kaladin among the singers — Kaladin follows a band of freed parshmen to Revolar, learns how they see the world, and escapes the Fused on a highstorm.
A fortified wooden stronghold with cannons at the far end of Patji, where the Ones Above set their machine.
The Ones Above’s device inside the trading company’s fort.
The tamed islands of the Eelakin, with their cities and reefs, about three weeks’ rowing from the Pantheon. Their layout here is our placeholder.
A frozen wasteland to the south of the homeisles, with native ravens and no sign of people.
The Father island, the largest of the Pantheon: wedge-shaped, with knife-edged peaks and a jungle that punishes every mistake. Aviar must visit it to gain their talents. Dusk traps here.
A green-tinted lake of not-quite-water in a canyon toward Patji’s eastern peak, holding glowing worms. It is a perpendicularity, and Dusk sails through it into the Emberdark.
A green-tinted pool of not-water full of glowing worms. Their paste lets things float in the emberdark, and the Aviar gain their talents from them.
The smallest and tamest island of the Pantheon, closest to home, where young trappers train.
A Nagadan city destroyed by nightmares decades before the story.
A Nagadan city; placed on the coast as a guess.
A round city in Nagadan laid out in rings and wedges beside a lake, built around a hion line, with the shroud on its west side. Nikaro paints nightmares here.
Yumi and Nikaro ride the Jotun Line here.
Glowing lines of power that run through the city and light it.
Design’s noodle stand, where Nikaro’s friends gather. Later it becomes the Noodle Princess.
The black shroud along the city’s west side. Painters patrol it at night and paint away the nightmares that come out; at the end Nikaro gathers thirty-seven painters here against an army of them.
Warm, humid springs where Yumi’s people lived, heated by the hijo under the ground, with gardens floating in the rising air. Beyond them lie the searing barrens and then the cold wastes.
Where Yumi stacks stones to draw the hijo, once calling a record thirty-seven at a time.
The village shrine where Yumi prays each day before her stacking.
The ruined capital of old Torio, west of Kilahito, with red roofs, fountains and dragon statues. The machine that made the shroud was switched on here.

In Torio City’s grand exhibit hall: the machine switched on at a Festival of Reveals long ago, which consumed the Torish people and made the shroud. Yumi stacks hundreds of stone towers to draw the spirits away until it stops.
Red spores that throw up spike-forests in sudden squalls. The dragon Xisis lies in a lair near its lunagree. It borders the Midnight Sea and is one of the few ways in.
The dragon’s lair near the crimson lunagree. Tress bargains here, and the spore-eating captain Crow is left in the dragon’s service.
The green Verdant Sea, Tress’s home sea, piled highest under its moon’s spore-fall.
Probably the royal city of the Verdant king, in the Core Archipelago far from the Rock. Position is our placeholder.
Large islands of the Sapphire Sea with a hunting culture; home of Fort and Salay.
Black, warm spores, walled in by mountains on four sides; the Sorceress’s domain.
A crooked finger of black saltstone in the Emerald Sea, 50 or 60 miles from the green lunagree, with a small town and the duke’s mansion near the top. Tress works here and collects cups.
Where the ships of the Emerald Sea call. Tress leaves from here as a stowaway to rescue Charlie.
Tress’s family home, where she keeps the cups that sailors trade her.
Near the top of the Rock: home of the duke and his son Charlie, Tress’s friend.
A pink, inhabited sea bordering the Emerald.
The blue Zephyr Sea in the north, home of the Islands of Lobu and the Zephyr Islands.
A small, suspiciously round island in the Midnight Sea near the Crimson border, with a silver tower that is really a starship.
The Sorceress’s tower, coated in silver, which turns out to be a starship.
The colourful river port of the Violet Duke, about two weeks by barge from Kingseat.
The capital at the summit of Mountaincrest, grown up around the skeletal corpse of the Megalith, from whose heart the three blood rivers flow.
Hexers mine demonstone from the river here; December spies on them.
The skeletal corpse of the demon the Prophet slew eight hundred years ago, with the city grown around it. Its blood runs out in the rivers.
King Beaudilog’s palace, which keeps the Prophet’s sword. December warns the court of plague here and is later caught and imprisoned.
A kingdom several months’ travel to the east.
A scholarly monastery about 800 years old where the Violet ends on the plains, with a great library on demons.
The monks’ great library on demons, where December spends years studying.
December’s home town on the River Violet, south of Duck Seat.
Where the orphan December grows up with the innkeeper’s family, and where she first sees Hoid.
One of the three rivers of the Megalith’s glowing blood, which December follows up the mountain.
The last sizeable city before the capital, about three days by barge.
A huge, flat forest south of Mountaincrest, humanity’s first home here, with nomad clans and giant walking demons.
The small capital of Idris in a mountain valley, Siri and Vivenna’s home.
The landlocked sea east of Hallandren, which Idrians call the Inner Sea.
A walled plateau in the south of T’Telir over the sea: a ring of palaces for the Returned and the God King’s black palace, where Siri is sent to be married.
A roofless sand arena behind the palaces, where priests debate before the gods and athletes compete.
Barracks for Hallandren’s army of Lifeless soldiers, controlled by gods who know the command phrases.
The Court is essentially one vast lawn inside its walls; gardeners lay out flowers when a god asks.
The God King’s black, stepped palace at the far end of the Court, where Siri is brought as his wife.
The Returned gods’ palaces stand around the Court’s lawn, including those of Lightsong and Blushweaver.
Passages under the Court, used by Bluefingers and his hidden forces.
A quiet field of hundreds of old warrior statues in the north of the city.
Hundreds of old warrior statues stand in the quiet D’Denir garden.
In a shadowy jungle cavern in Hallandren; its seeping Investiture feeds the Tears of Edgli flowers. Worldhoppers pass customs here. The exact site is not given.
Northern kingdoms beyond the Idrian mountains, destroyed in the Manywar.
A quiet southern province of tropical lowlands inside Hallandren, with grievances of its own.
Idris controls four trade passes north through its mountains and lives on their tolls.
The kingdom directly across the Bright Sea, friendly with Idris and at odds with Hallandren since the Manywar.
Hallandren’s capital, built in a crescent around a sheltered bay on the Bright Sea, with markets, merchant mansions, slums and docks, and Awakened statues everywhere.
Shipyards, warehouses and slums along the bay.
The Idrian quarter called the Highlands, where Vivenna meets the slumlords Paxen, Ashu, and Rira.
Brightly colored crowds fill the city’s streets.
The city wall, with gates carved as sea creatures.
A barren island chain beyond the Aimian Sea, homeland of the Aimians.
The ancient Aimian capital ringed by Soulcast spikes, hiding the real Oathgate and a Dawnshard. The Dawnshard expedition sails here.
The real Oathgate, hidden in the forbidden city, where the expedition finds something far older than the Radiants.
Soulcast spikes ringing the forbidden old Aimian capital.
Azir’s capital, with the Bronze Palace and the Grand Market dome over the Makabakam Oathgate. Lift steals food here; Azir is run by scribes and forms.
An indoor market under a great bronze dome, built over the city’s Oathgate. The Azish fortify it once they learn what is underneath.
The platform under the market dome, which Lift unlocks to open the way to Urithiru.
Seat of the Prime Aqasix. Lift breaks in to steal food, and the boy Gawx, whom she heals, is chosen as Prime.
A dusty mining region at the eastern end of the Mountains of Ur; Shallan’s family’s lands are near.
Where Roshar has land, Shadesmar has an ocean of glass beads, each the soul of an object. Sink in and you may not come back.
A big spren trading port on the west side of the ‘island’ that mirrors the Sea of Spears. The travellers from Kholinar buy passage here.
A busy spren trading port on the bead sea. The travellers from Kholinar buy passage here on a ship bound toward Thaylen.
Cold, lawless lands south of the Plains, scoured by the strongest storms.
Kaladin’s home town beside a breakwall hill, where his father was the surgeon.
The citylord’s manor. Roshone’s feud with Lirin shapes Kaladin’s childhood.
The surgeon’s house where Kaladin grew up learning his father’s trade.
A humid land of long peninsulas north of Jah Keved; Lopen’s home, occupied by the singers.
Crater-topped mountains holding warm emerald lakes, home of the Unkalaki. Rock comes from here.
Warm lakes in the mountains’ crater tops where the Unkalaki live; Rock speaks of their spren and their peaks.
A major Alethi city at the Deathbend delta on the Tarat Sea.
An Iriali city on a bay where the great spren Cusicesh rises from the water each morning.
Every morning the great spirit Cusicesh rises from the bay at the same minute, and the people come to watch.
Just before Stormfall Cusicesh speaks to the Iriali for the first time and opens a perpendicularity, and they leave Roshar through it.
Axies the Collector, studying spren, ends up drunk, robbed and locked up here.
A city-state built up a mountainside in a wedge harbour on the Tarat Sea, with the Palanaeum library dug beneath it. Shallan finds Jasnah here; its king is Taravangian.
Jasnah walks into a dark alley knowing she will be attacked, and Soulcasts the four thugs who follow her while Shallan watches.
The City of Bells: chimes all over the city ring the hours and warn of highstorms.
The king’s palace, dug into the mountain at the top of the city. Here Taravangian reveals to Szeth that he holds his oathstone and sends him after Dalinar.
A natural wedge harbour on the Tarat Sea. Shallan arrives here on the Wind’s Pleasure, and leaves on it with Jasnah.
Kharbranth’s hospitals are famous across Roshar, and its surgeons go wherever there is war.
The greatest library on Roshar, beneath the Conclave. Shallan finds Jasnah studying here and talks her way into becoming her ward.
The switchback road climbing from the harbour to the Conclave.
Alethkar’s capital, built among storm-carved rock fins. Gavilar was murdered in his palace here, and the city falls to the singers in Oathbringer. Its Oathgate was corrupted by the Unmade Sja-anat.
Azure’s headquarters, where a hidden Soulcaster in an aluminium-lined room keeps soldiers and refugees fed. Kaladin joins the Guard here.
The Oathgate platform, joined to the palace by the Sunwalk and used as the ardents’ monastery. Its spren has been corrupted by Sja-anat, and the Cult of Moments holds endless feasts on it.

head_text: The Kholin palace. King Gavilar is murdered here on the night of the treaty feast.
About sixty feet high, built into the windblades. Highmarshal Azure’s Wall Guard holds it against Fused raids until a thunderclast breaks through.

head_text: Sleek, layered rock formations in Kholinar.
A tailor’s house where Elhokar, Adolin, Kaladin and Shallan hide while they work out how to reach the Oathgate.
The City of Lightning on an island off Rira’s east coast, site of an Oathgate.
The City of Lightning on its island holds one of the ten Oathgates.
The honorspren capital, a tall roofless box of blue stone on a cliff over the Astral Banks, where each inner wall has its own gravity. Adolin stands trial here.
Adolin’s party camps outside the closed fortress, waiting for the honorspren to let him in.
Adolin stands trial here for the betrayal of the ancient Radiants, and calls on the dead spren of his Blade as a witness.
A tall, roofless box of blue stone. Each inner wall has its own gravity, and the honorspren live on all four.
The range that breaks the highstorms before they reach Shinovar.
The old Natanatan capital at the centre of the Plains, the listeners’ stronghold, with an Oathgate on a plateau to its south-west.
One of four fortresses Sigzil and Bridge Four build on Narak to hold the Plains through the ten days of the contest. It is the first to fall.
The central stronghold and the last line on the Plains, stormed by Venli’s chasmfiends at the end of the defence.
The third fortress, lost on the seventh day.
The fortress Sigzil falls back to after Narak One is lost, and holds while Narak Three falls.
A round plateau south-west of Narak, its gate hidden under centuries of crem. Shallan finds the mechanism and carries the trapped armies away to Urithiru.
Ruined Natanatan buildings at the heart of the Plains where the listeners make their stronghold. Here Eshonai’s people sing in the new forms that call the Everstorm.
The last remnant of the old Natanatan kingdom on the eastern coast.
Obsidian ground over the Southern Depths; voidspren ships first appeared near it.
Obsidian highlands where the Reshi Sea lies in the Physical Realm, between the three great seas.
Obsidian ground over the north-western ocean, the road toward Sel’s subastral.
Urithiru in the Cognitive Realm: a glowing pillar of crystallised Investiture.
Urithiru’s reflection in Shadesmar: a glowing column of crystallised Investiture.
Far east across the Ocean of Origins, where the highstorms are born. No map shows it.
Babatharnam’s capital and the old Sela Tales Oathgate. Its position inside the country is our guess.
Babatharnam’s capital holds the Oathgate of the old kingdom of Sela Tales.
A crater lake in the Horneater Peaks: Roshar’s stable doorway into Shadesmar and the usual way worldhoppers arrive. It vanished when Cultivation left in Wind and Truth.
A crater lake that opens into Shadesmar, the usual way worldhoppers come to Roshar.
A warm, ankle-deep lake hundreds of miles across, with stilt villages of the Purelakers.
Home of the fisherman Ishikk, who is paid by three strange foreigners to search the lake for a man who sounds very like Wit.
Purelakers live in villages raised above the warm, ankle-deep water and fish it from rafts.
The City of Shadows in Iri, under a mountain overhang, with an Oathgate in a round reservoir.
The City of Shadows lies under a mountain overhang; its Oathgate sits in a round reservoir.
A canyon city at the north tip of the Sea of Spears, burned by Dalinar in his years as the Blackthorn.
The canyon city that rebels against Gavilar. In Dalinar’s memories he burns it to the ground, not knowing that his wife Evi is inside.
Hot equatorial islands in the Reshi Sea, some of them living greatshells. Talik comes from here.
A living greatshell island. Rysn climbs down its head on a rope to plead with the island itself; the rope breaks and she falls, and the island gives her a live larkin.
Roshar’s largest sea, a bay cutting deep into the north coast.
One of the largest cities of Highprince Vamah’s lands.
Where the singers keep their human captives and assign them labour. Moash is held here after his capture.
Army barracks and parshman quarters on the east side, where tens of thousands of singers gather after the Everstorm.
Highprince Vamah’s seat sprawls up the slopes of a hollow; the original city walls now only mark its inner districts.
A stone tower with a heatless bonfire on a peninsula of obsidian that is a river in the Physical Realm. Its exact counterpart is our guess.
A stone tower with a fire that gives no heat. Kaladin looks into it and sees Thaylen City overrun and Dalinar surrounded.
The eastern bead sea, over Alethkar, Jah Keved, Herdaz and the Frostlands. Kaladin, Shallan and Adolin cross it from Kholinar.
The western bead sea, over Shinovar and Iri.
The central bead sea, over Azir, the Ur range and the southern kingdoms. The honorspren lands are on it.
A wide, shallow lake bristling with rock spires.
A city sunk into drainage gashes in a stone plain, fought over by Emul and Tukar.
A slave-trading port linked to the warcamps by caravan.
Plateaus split by deep chasms, where the Alethi warcamps hunt chasmfiends for gemhearts. The fragments of a fourth moon that fell long ago lie beneath. Kaladin runs bridges here as a slave.
Deep cracks between the plateaus, flooded by every highstorm. Bridge Four is sent down to scavenge from the dead, and Kaladin secretly trains his men with spears here.
Toward the east the chasms widen and the plateaus break into impassable pillars, the way the listeners came and went.

A chasm a short walk from Sadeas’s warcamp, the one place bridgemen may go unwatched, and where despairing bridgemen jump. Kaladin comes here meaning to end it, and Syl talks him into trying once more.
Chasmfiends climb up onto the plateaus to pupate, and the highprinces race each other across the chasms to cut out the gemhearts. Bridge crews run ahead under listener arrows, carrying the bridges.
Grass that stays still, soil and upright trees, sheltered from the highstorms behind the Misted Mountains. The Shin will not walk on stone. Szeth’s homeland.
The last stop. Ishar raises corrupted Honorbearers against them, Kaladin speaks the Fifth Ideal and frees Ishar, and Szeth fights with Nightblood.
Szeth’s family home, seen in his memories.
Where Szeth finds that his sister Elid holds the Honorblade, and the two are reconciled.
Soft soil, grass that does not hide and trees that stand straight, all sheltered by the mountains. The Shin hold stone sacred and will not walk on it.
Where Szeth recovers Shalash’s Honorblade.
Kaladin and Szeth come through a pass in the Misted Mountains into the lush lands beyond.
Kaladin duels the Herald Nale here; Nale yields his Honorblade and admits what Ishar has done.
Szeth kills the corrupted stone shaman here and takes back Taln’s Honorblade.
The gulf between Alethkar, Jah Keved and the Frostlands; its outlet is Longbrow’s Straits.
The terraced capital of Thaylenah on the main island’s north-west coast, with the Thalath Oathgate. The Battle of Thaylen Field ends Oathbringer.
The docks and market district outside the wall, wrecked by the Everstorm. Odium’s armies and the possessed Sadeas troops fight here, and Dalinar faces Odium.
On the north-east edge beside the Royal Ward, long used as a sculpture garden, until it is cleared and reopened to Urithiru.
Seat of the Thaylen monarchs and of Queen Fen.
The national bank, which holds the great gemstone called the King’s Drop. The thunderclast Yushah smashes it during the battle.
An ancient carved stone kept in the city. Its translation says humans came to Roshar as the invaders, and the coalition nearly breaks apart over it.
One of ten Herald temples in the Royal Ward. Dalinar finds his Bondsmith power when he mends a broken statue and this damaged temple, and Queen Fen joins his coalition.
Runs north to south below the city. Breached in the battle; the gap is later sealed with Soulcast metal.
Thaylenah’s main island seen from Shadesmar: a ‘sea’ of obsidian ground, with the Oathgate dais just offshore on a single bridge.
The Shadesmar side of Thaylen City’s Oathgate, reached by a single bridge. Its spren refuse to let the travellers through.
A huge plateau where Sadeas abandons Dalinar’s army and Bridge Four turns back to save it.
An enormous plateau where chasmfiends like to pupate. Sadeas pulls his men back across the chasm here and leaves Dalinar’s army to die, and Bridge Four turns back to bring them out.
The theocracy of the god-priest Tezim, who is really the Herald Ishar.
An honorspren stronghold near where Kharbranth stands.
The ten-tiered tower city of the ancient Radiants, carved from a mountain high in the Mountains of Ur, home of the Sibling and hub of the ten Oathgates.
A room where the ancient Radiants stored their records inside gemstones.
The cavernous central market hall on the lower levels, where merchants and refugees fill the once-empty tower.
A water chamber in the tower where Dalinar opens a perpendicularity and goes with Navani into the Spiritual Realm.
Miles of lightless, half-explored passages. Sadeas’s body is found in a corridor, and more killings follow.
A chamber near the top with a great map table, where Dalinar plans his coalition’s war.
A fourth-floor hospital for the wounded in mind, where Kaladin, retired from fighting, works with the patients.
Ten platforms on the plaza before the tower, each linked to an Oathgate across Roshar. Shallan’s gate from Narak brings the Alethi armies here at the end of Words of Radiance.
A pillar of gemstones deep in the tower, the heart of the Sibling. Raboniel pours Voidlight into it to seize the tower; Navani later bonds the Sibling here and becomes a Bondsmith.
A hidden ground-floor chamber where the Unmade Re-Shephir lurks. Shallan confronts her here with Lightweaving and drives her off.
A hot, overgrown valley where the Nightwatcher grants boons and curses. Dalinar sought her here; Lift asked to stay young.
A warm, overgrown valley where people come to the Old Magic for a boon and a curse. Taravangian’s boon from her shapes everything he does.
Jah Keved’s clifftop capital on the Tarat Sea, torn by succession war. Its Oathgate platform became a palace garden.
The ancient centre is laid out as a hexagon with matching streets, and it has a temple for every Vorin devotary.
The city stands above a ridge guarding its port. In the Battle of Vedenar one army is driven over the cliffs, and the docks are burned.
Farmland north of the walls, where the war dead were burned.
The Oathgate dais had become a palace garden. Reopened by Malata, it links Vedenar to Urithiru again.
King Hanavanar holds a feast meant as a trap for the Assassin in White, and Szeth kills him anyway.
Ten craters along the western rim, one per highprince. North to south: Roion, Sadeas, Aladar, Kholin, Vamah, Ruthar, Thanadal, Hatham, Bethab, Sebarial.
Where Adolin duels for Shardblades to win his father’s cause. One match turns into four Shardbearers against him, until Kaladin jumps into the ring.
A plain stone barrack in Sadeas’s camp, home of the bridge crew given the worst duties. Kaladin is tied to its outside wall and left to a highstorm, and he lives.

A shallow bowl at the foot of the Pinnacle that is flooded for feasts, so its five round platforms become islands joined by bridges. The king’s Wit sits by the entrance insulting guests, and the highprinces scheme over spiced food.
Orderly barracks in rings around Dalinar’s bunker-like complex. During highstorms he is tied down in his rooms while the visions take him.
An unplanned sprawl of shops beside the palace hill, run largely by Thaylen merchants and patrolled by Kholin scribes.
King Elhokar’s Soulcast palace on a hill ringed by a sheer drop, the centre of Alethi government on the Plains. The king meets his highprinces in its conference chamber.
The least ordered of the ten camps, where the slave bridge crews are kept and spent on the plateau runs.
The southernmost camp and the most practical, with farms, trade and running water. Shallan lodges here when she reaches the Plains.
A Tashikki city made of Shardblade-cut trenches spiralling to the Grand Indicium, where Lift faces the Herald Nale in Edgedancer.

head_text: A guarded entrance with a long line of people waiting to enter; Lift sneaks toward the front.
A huge records building towering over the city. Lift talks her way in as an envoy from Azir to find who Darkness is hunting.
Lift watches the man she calls Darkness execute a girl here for stealing fruit.
The city’s deep cut channels, where farmers grow crops out of season.
Caves north of Luthadel where Kelsier’s skaa army trained.
Where Kelsier’s skaa army hides and drills.
A fieldstone fortress near the highest Seran peaks, with trapped corridors guarding the Bands.
Passages full of traps that the team disarms, only for Wax’s uncle to open the last door for the Set. The vault is empty.
Marasi realises the temple is a decoy: the real Bands were reforged as the spearhead of a statue.
The Basin’s other great port, on a peninsula, with the tower called the Shaw. The Set’s stronghold in The Lost Metal.
The Basin’s other great port.
The tower at the heart of Bilming, stronghold of the Set.
A broadsheet in The Lost Metal reports a perfectly blue pool here; it may be Harmony’s perpendicularity, which canon places only in the far south.
A windowless, steel-plated fortress of the Steel Inquisitors in a crater south-east of Luthadel.
Sazed and Marsh find a massacre here, and a steel plate engraved with Kwaan’s words, which Sazed copies by rubbing.
The biggest rail junction outside Elendel, built where an ashmount once stood.
A rail city far north-east of Elendel, on the line to the Northern Roughs.
A remote farming village at the foot of the Seran Range.
Hides a damaged flying ship from the south. Marasi frees its masked prisoner, Allik, and the team escapes in a smaller craft.
Capital of the Basin, split into eight octants by canals around the Field of Rebirth, on Hammondar Bay. The equator runs close by and the prime meridian through it.
On the suspension tower of this bridge Wax corners Bleeder, who wears Lessie’s face.
The park at the centre of the eight octants, with a museum and tomb. Wax gets in through a secret door in its atium chamber.
Bleeder breaks into the safe room here, and Wax later works out she has taken the governor’s place.
The near-bankrupt house Wax inherits when he comes back from the Roughs.
Raised by the city after The Lost Metal.
The Terris enclave where Wax’s grandmother lived.
A western capital ringed by red rock formations, guarding one of the Lord Ruler’s storage caches. Besieged in The Hero of Ages.
One of the Lord Ruler’s storage caverns, the reason the crew comes.
At a ball here Elend gives King Yomen an ultimatum, and Yomen refuses.
Rock walls and a canyon-like approach make the city hard to take. Elend’s army besieges it, and Yomen’s raid destroys half his koloss.
A large Northern Roughs city.
A genteel town an hour from Luthadel, where the crew set up the Renoux mansion.
The crew’s front: a rented mansion where Vin learns to play the noblewoman Valette.
The atium mines, worked by skaa prisoners, where Kelsier survived and Snapped. Ruin’s pool lay below them.
Prisoners crawl into the cracks to find atium geodes and seldom last a year. Kelsier survived here when his wife did not. At the end of the trilogy Elend makes his last stand here against the koloss.
In The Hero of Ages the Terris people shelter here, and none of them die of the mist sickness.
The kandra’s cavern city near the Pits, where the Lord Ruler’s atium was hidden.
Where TenSoon is sentenced to starve, and from which he escapes.
A round, metal-walled chamber lit by oil lamps, the kandra’s court and holiest place. TenSoon is tried here; the Lord Ruler’s atium, the Trust, lies hidden beneath its platform.
Islands across the Southern Sea from the Final Empire.
The Lord Ruler’s palace, the Hill of a Thousand Spires, where Vin finally faces him.
A dome painted with a mountain, a cavern, a pool of light and something dark, around a small old building with a carved door.
Towers and iron rods of every thickness; the palace has no outer walls. At the end Vin, holding Preservation’s power, fights Ruin’s last Inquisitors here and the palace is crushed into the ground.
Vin is questioned here after her capture. She comes back crashing through a stained-glass window and kills the Lord Ruler.
A southern capital on the Channerel, destroyed by lava near the end.
Capital of the Final Empire, walled, with eight gates named for metals, and the River Channerel running through it. It was built over the Well of Ascension.
Where Elend’s new Assembly meets, and votes him off his own throne during the siege.

head_text: The river that runs through the city.
A raised square with four fountains where the Lord Ruler stages executions and every man must watch. Kelsier dies in a courtyard beside it, and it becomes the Square of the Survivor.
Another noble keep. During the siege Vin and Zane spar across its heights, and Elend dines here with Lord Cett.

head_text: Luthadel's defensive walls, where Elend watches Straff Venture's approaching army.
Our estimate of where Luthadel’s ruins lie in the remade world, from overlaying the two maps; no book map marks it.
A terraced waterfall city with gondolas on the southern edge of the Basin.
A city built down a waterfall, crossed by gondolas. At a party here Wax is framed for the murder of Lady Kelesina Shores.
The Festival City on the Sea of Lennes, at the edge of the Conrad Delta in the Southern Roughs.
A city north-east of Elendel on the railway toward the Faleast Range, outside Elendel’s control.
Near the south pole, across a wide ocean: colder and harsher than the Basin, with towers and flying craft. Home of the Malwish and other southern peoples, revealed in The Bands of Mourning.
An eastern mining city with a storage cache.
A city due east of Elendel along the Irongate.
A Terris city in the foothills of the Channerel Range.
Capital of the Terris people in the far north, seat of the Keepers’ Synod. Burned by koloss.
The Western Dominance’s old capital, a market city of luxuries.
The largest city of the Northern Roughs, where two rivers meet; the only railhead out there.
A large lake west of Luthadel with an ashmount rising from its middle.
The sea in the Northern Roughs that took the place of Lake Tyrian.
Capital of the Northern Dominance and the Ventures’ seat, its streets drained canals. Held by rebel skaa in The Hero of Ages.
The Citizen executes nobles by locking them in buildings and burning them. Spook finds the hidden ways out.
The storage cavern under the city, found by Spook and Sazed’s team.
The city’s streets are drained canals; their water was diverted to an underground lake that hides the Lord Ruler’s cache.
A southern farming and mining town with a cache under its Ministry building.
A dusty grassland town in the Roughs, Waxillium’s base for twenty years.
Preservation’s perpendicularity: a small pool of glowing power in a cavern beneath the palace. Rashek moved it here from the Terris mountains.
A pool of liquid power in a cavern beneath the palace, behind a hidden door. Vin releases its power instead of using it, and something escapes.
The lake near the centre of Arelon, fed by rivers from the south-west and drained north-east by the Aredel. It is the dot in Aon Aon.
The range between Arelon and Fjorden, called Dathreki in Fjorden, which long held off the Derethi armies.
The great crack across southern Arelon opened by the Reod earthquake, beside the Kalomo River. Raoden realises the Aons echo the shape of the land and need a chasm line to work again.
The Chasm is the feature whose missing line Raoden adds to his Aons.
Derethi monastery of the bone-warriors, somewhere in Fjorden; the exact site is not given.
A vast desert south of all the known nations of Opelon.
The swampy province of the Bloodsealers.

The shining city of the Elantrians in north-east Arelon, near the coast and the northern end of the Atad Mountains. After the Reod its walls hold the Shaod’s victims; Raoden is thrown in here at the start of the book.
Those taken by the Shaod are confined within Elantris; Raoden enters through this gate.
Elantris’s high walls now serve to keep its people in.
Capital of Duladel, near the Atad passes and the borders of Arelon and Fjorden.
A rural backwater in the empire’s south-east.
Arelon’s second city under King Iadon, on Duke Roial’s lands. Which coast it is on is not stated; this placement is ours.
A landlocked nation of the empire between JinDo and Hraggen, with the desert to the south.
A land south-east of Arelon, related in culture to MaiPon. The city of HaiKo lies in its north-east.

The eastern gate city beside Elantris, on the Aredel’s mouth and Arelon’s best northern harbour. It became the capital after the Reod. Elantris and its four gate cities (Ake, Ato, Kae and Toa) together form the Aon Rao.
King Iadon’s palace in Kae. Sarene meets him here after arriving from Teod.
A southern Arelene city on the Chasm.
A town on the Aredel River, about halfway between Elantris and Lake Alonoe.
Shai’s homeland and the heart of Forgery; its position in the empire is not given.
A mountainous province of the Rose Empire whose Strikers guard the passes to Teod.
A small, deep pool of thick, crystalline blue liquid in the Atad Mountains south-east of Elantris, reached by tunnel or switchbacks.
Capital of the Rose Empire on the northern continent, built on seven hills with the Rose Palace on the centre one. Here Shai rebuilds the emperor’s soul in The Emperor’s Soul.
The guarded room where Shai spends her hundred days carving soulstamps to rebuild the emperor, with the arbiter Gaotona watching.
On the central of the capital’s seven hills: the seat of the emperor and the arbiters.
Svorden’s capital and harbour at the north-east tip of Opelon, the empire’s northernmost point; Sarene once served here as ambassador.
Capital of Teod, Sarene’s homeland, a forest-ringed port across the Sea of Fjorden. Its navy rules the sea.
The largest city of Geant, on the river border with Svorden.
Capital of Fjorden and of the Fjordell Empire, a northern port and the seat of the Wyrn, whose Derethi church sends Hrathen west to Arelon.
The books describe Silverlight mostly through its scholars and its rules. This surface is our own interpretation.
The ocean ring along the line between day and night, with a permanent storm along its middle that makes crossings deadly.
The night face, always turned to the dim Eye of Ridos and lit in ultraviolet twilight. Khriss comes from the nation of Elis here, which resists the Dynasty. Its shape is our placeholder.
Uninhabited deep desert east of Lossand, home of the deep sandlings.
The capital of Kerzta, the largest and strongest Dayside nation, due west of Kezare.
A sand ‘lake’ with water just beneath and vines under the surface, ringing KraeDa and covering much of Kerzta.
Lossand’s capital, on river islands where the Ry’DoAli meets the Nor’Tallon. Home of the Diem, the order of Sand Masters, in a building carved from one block of white sandstone.
The home of the Sand Masters, carved from a single block of white sandstone.
A lone mountain at the exact centre of Dayside, with the sun directly overhead. Kerla’s sand surrounds it, and the Diem hold their trials at its foot.
A port at the mouth of the Ry’DoAli on the south coast, where the sun sits low on the horizon.
Capital of Tallon, in the mountains that wall off the eastern Rim Kingdoms.
An extraordinarily deep trench in the ocean between the continents, mentioned in Tress.
Another fortress town in the mountains.
The larger continent, humanity’s first home on Threnody, consumed by the Evil. Expeditions there do not come back.
The smaller continent, almost wall-to-wall forest, unnaturally silent and haunted by shades. No fire, no blood: the Simple Rules keep you alive.
The most powerful fortress town on the forested continent, which posts the bounties. Position is our placeholder.
A rickety bridge over a chasm near the waystop; the wreck of the New Bridge lies below it.
A rickety span over a chasm; the wreck of the New Bridge lies below.
Silence Montane’s roadside inn on the forest road, ringed by three circles of silver. Its position is our placeholder.
The inn Silence keeps for travellers on the forest road, paid for by her secret bounty hunting.
Three circles of silver around the waystop keep the shades out.

Regions overrun by bone-white invasive life; about half the trees are white.
A glowing hole high in Yolen’s atmosphere where the Silverlight Nexus comes through, with a flying city of dragons nearby. Its position on the globe is our placeholder.
Somewhere on Yolen, eighteen conspirators struck down Adonalsium with a weapon made from the Dawnshards. The exact place has never been shown.
The space beside the green crystal, where the Falcon studies it (marker position schematic).

A faintly green crystal the size of a planet, orbiting a white dwarf. It reacts to the Falcon’s live protomolecule sample, and Elvi suspects it stores records; the mission commander forces them on before she can finish.
Elvi’s team sends Cara, and then Cara and Amos together, into the diamond’s memory. They see the builders’ history, until Amos persuades Elvi to stop using Cara.
Elvi Okoye’s Laconian science ship, exploring the dead systems with her husband Fayez and their team.
The capital, with the governor’s office and a great agricultural company (spelled Barradon in some places; position estimated).
Auberon accepts the new order early, and Duarte sends it a Laconian governor who rules from here.
Stranded when Laconia halts gate traffic, Naomi reaches Auberon and takes over its Underground, then gathers ships from across the colonies.
Another of Auberon’s cities (position estimated).
The colony world of the system, with an orbital complex above it (marker position estimated).
Having followed the wrong ship here, Tanaka has her wounds treated and looks for help, and medication, for the memories in her head that are not her own.
Twin shipyards (position estimated), struck in the opening raid of the fifth book.
Filip Inaros’s team knocks out the yard’s defences and steals four canisters of stealth coating, leaving two of their own men behind.
Inside the rock (marker position schematic): the busy ports of the Belt’s biggest station.
Mars sues for the return of its stolen corvette, and the Rocinante is held here. Holden takes a documentary contract to pay the lawyers.
Naomi meets her son Filip here and buys the small transport Chetzemoka for his crew. As she says goodbye, Marco’s people seize her, as planned all along.
Inside the rock (marker position schematic): the seat of Anderson Dawes, governor of Ceres under the Free Navy.

Marco Inaros tells Governor Dawes he will strip Ceres of its reactors, defences and medical supplies and leave its millions to his enemies. When Filip shoots a Ceres security officer, Dawes confronts Marco.
Inside the rock (marker position schematic): the precinct where Miller is handed the Julie Mao case as a side job, and later fired.
Star Helix Security’s precinct. Miller’s captain quietly hands him the Julie Mao job here, and later takes his badge when he will not let it go.
Ceres’s corridors and levels, where Miller works his beat. Riots break out across the Belt after Holden’s broadcast blames Mars.
