Where the Thirty Worlds expedition to Earth begins (marker position estimated; the epilogue gives no detail of the planet).
About a thousand years after the gates fall, the Thirty Worlds have built their own faster-than-light ship. An expedition sets out to find old Earth.
The Nigerian capital, where Anna Volovodov’s wife Namono lives through the aftermath of the rocks at the start of the sixth book.
Where Amos grew up on the streets. He comes back for the funeral of the woman who raised him and meets his old friend Erich.
Amos’s childhood friend Erich runs the local criminal trade from here. After the rocks fall, Erich leaves Earth with Amos and Clarissa.
The first of the Free Navy’s rocks comes down over Africa. Other impacts devastate regions of North America, West Africa and South Asia (exact sites are not given; marker estimated).
Where one of the Free Navy’s stealth-coated rocks comes down (exact place not given). The impacts and their aftermath kill vast numbers and break Earth’s ecology.
Holden grew up on a family farm co-op in Montana with several parents (the exact place is not given; marker estimated).
The co-op where Holden was raised by a family of eight parents (exact place not given).
The UN capital, home of the Secretariat, where Chrisjen Avasarala plays the politics of Earth.
The seat of Earth’s government. Avasarala works its offices, and Bobbie Draper, brought to Earth for the peace talks, ends up on her staff here.
Amos visits the widower of the woman who raised him.
A rich enclave with a private launch pad. After the rocks fall, Amos, Clarissa and Erich get a shuttle off the ground here and make for Luna.
A wealthy enclave’s own launch pad. Amos, Clarissa and Erich get a shuttle off the broken Earth from here and make for Luna.
Inside the station (marker position schematic): Holden’s crew and Miller fight their way out of the dying station.
Miller drags a sickening Holden back here, and the Rocinante gets them out of the dying station; the ship’s medical bay treats their radiation.
Inside the station (marker position schematic): where Miller and Holden find Julie Mao’s body, overgrown by something that is not human.
A cheap hotel room where Miller and Holden’s crew find Julie Mao dead, her body overgrown by a strange growth. Her records point to the ship that brought the infection.
Inside the station (marker position schematic): a fake radiation alarm herds the people of Eros here, where they are infected.

Behind the false radiation alarm, the shelters really are flooded with lethal radiation, and the people herded inside are seeded with the protomolecule. Holden and Miller force their way in and are badly dosed.
The settlement where Anna Volovodov lives with her wife Nono and their daughter Nami (marker position estimated).
Anna is a Methodist pastor here. She leaves her family to join the UN’s delegation of artists and clergy sent to witness the Ring.

The Canterbury — The ice hauler Canterbury, out of Saturn’s rings for Ceres, answers a distress call from a derelict ship, the Scopuli. Its executive officer Jim Holden takes four crew to look. While they are away a stealth ship destroys the Canterbury, and Holden broadcasts that Martian technology was involved.
A side job for Miller — On Ceres, the tired detective Joe Miller is quietly told to find Julie Mao, the runaway daughter of a rich Lunar family, and send her home. Riots follow Holden’s broadcast.
The Rocinante reaches Tycho — After escaping the destruction of the Donnager, Holden’s crew reaches Fred Johnson’s station.
Miller fired — Miller learns Julie had joined the OPA and was aboard the Scopuli. Warned off, he keeps digging, loses his badge, and buys passage to Eros.
Julie — Miller meets Holden’s crew on Eros. They find Julie dead in a hotel room, covered in a strange growth, and her records point to the ship that brought the infection.
The Eros incident — A false radiation alarm herds the people of Eros into shelters, where Protogen seeds them with the protomolecule. Miller and the crew barely get out.

What came from Phoebe — A recording from Protogen reveals the truth: the protomolecule came from Phoebe, a weapon sent long ago to remake life on Earth. Eros is an experiment, and the Canterbury was destroyed to start a war that would keep everyone looking away.
Thoth Station — The crew, Miller and the OPA storm Protogen’s hidden station. Its chief scientist, Dresden, talks of making humanity into gods; Miller shoots him dead.
Into Venus — Miller rides a bomb into Eros and finds what is left of Julie steering it. He talks her round, and Eros comes down on Venus instead of Earth.

The Donnager — The Martian flagship Donnager picks up Holden’s crew and is then boarded by attackers. As the battleship is scuttled, the survivors escape in its gunship Tachi, which Holden renames the Rocinante.
Out of Eros — Badly dosed with radiation, Miller hauls Holden back to the Rocinante, and the ship’s medical bay keeps them both alive.
The assault on Thoth — Fred Johnson’s OPA attacks Protogen’s hidden station in space and inside its corridors. The Rocinante is badly damaged and has to set down on the station itself.
Repairs at Tycho — While the Rocinante is repaired at Tycho, Holden and Naomi become a couple, and the crew argues over what to do about Eros.
A bargaining chip — Back on Ceres, Holden gives Fred Johnson the protomolecule sample recovered from Protogen, to bargain with at the coming peace talks.
The monster on Ganymede — A creature wearing no armour wipes out Bobbie Draper’s Martian marine platoon and the UN troops facing them. Earth and Mars start shooting, and Ganymede comes apart.
Prax’s search — The botanist Prax Meng’s little daughter Mei has been taken from her school by her own doctor. Holden, Amos and Prax trace her to a hidden lab, and the thing kept inside it.
Avasarala — Bobbie is brought to Earth for peace talks and breaks ranks. Chrisjen Avasarala, a sharp-tongued UN official, takes her on and starts pulling at a conspiracy inside her own government.
Stowaway — A hybrid hidden in the Rocinante’s hold is killed with the ship’s own drive. At Tycho, Holden accuses Fred Johnson and the crew is cut loose from the OPA.

Escape from the Guanshiyin — Sent out on Jules-Pierre Mao’s yacht as a way of sidelining her, Avasarala learns a fleet is coming to kill Holden. Bobbie takes the yacht by force and they get to the Rocinante.

The battle over Io — The hybrids are made on Io, sold by Mao to a rogue UN faction. Holden boards the flagship of Admiral Nguyen to stop hybrid-loaded rockets bound for Mars, while Amos and Prax rescue Mei.
Venus rises — The structure on Venus finishes and launches itself out of the system. Aboard the Rocinante, Holden sees Miller again: a ghost made by the protomolecule.
Mei is taken — Four-year-old Mei Meng, who has an immune disorder, is led out of her preschool by her own doctor, Strickland. Other children with her condition vanish too.
The mirror falls — In the fighting one of the great mirrors comes down. Prax’s crops die, and the food system of the outer planets begins to fail.
The hunters beaten — With Martian warships alongside and Bobbie on the guns, the Rocinante beats the UN ships sent to kill Holden and turns for Io.
Mei found — Bobbie holds off a hybrid outside the lab while Prax and Amos go in. Prax finds Mei alive among the surviving children, and Amos kills Strickland.
The Ring — The construction from Venus stops beyond the orbit of Uranus and becomes a ring a thousand kilometres across. A young Belter racer dives through it and is lost, and the navies gather.
Anna — Anna Volovodov, a Methodist pastor from Europa, joins a UN delegation of artists and clergy sent to witness the Ring.
The Rocinante impounded — Mars sues for the return of its stolen corvette. Holden agrees to a documentary to pay the lawyers, and a film crew comes aboard.

Framed — Clarissa Mao, posing as a technician, hijacks the Rocinante through planted software and blames Holden for a bombing. With the fleets firing on him, Holden flies into the Ring, and the others follow.

The station — Inside is the slow zone. Holden reaches the station with Miller’s ghost and sees what happened to the builders: an empire across the galaxy, attacked by something, burning whole star systems to stop it.

Ashford’s gamble — Ashford orders the comm laser fired at the Ring, and Holden fears the station will answer by destroying the Sun. Moved by Anna’s broadcast, Clarissa opens the bridge, knocks Ashford from the controls and sends the Behemoth dark.
The gates open — The ships power down, the station judges them harmless, and the speed limit lifts. More than thirteen hundred gates open onto other star systems.

The slow zone — On the far side of the Ring, the torpedo chasing the Rocinante is caught and stopped. Nothing may move faster than six hundred metres a second, and the Behemoth leads the flotilla through after Holden.
The grenade — Martian marines follow Holden to the station, and one of them fires a grenade. The station answers by dropping its speed limit at a stroke.
Clarissa — Caught after attacking the Rocinante, Clarissa Mao is held in the Behemoth’s brig. Anna visits her and offers a forgiveness she will not accept.

First Landing — Refugees from Ganymede slip through a gate and found a mining town on Ilus. When a corporate survey ship arrives with a UN charter, they blow up its landing pad as a shuttle comes down.
Murtry — The corporate security chief Adolphus Murtry shoots a colonist in front of the town. Holden’s mediation fails as killings mount on both sides.

The planet wakes — An alien reactor melts down on the largest island. A storm of water and wind flattens the town; the survivors shelter in the ruins, and the planet’s old defences start shooting down anything with power.
Falling orbits — With their reactors dead, the ships in orbit start to fall. The Rocinante and the corporate ship’s crew rescue the refugees aboard the Barbapiccola before it burns up.

The dead spot — Guided by Miller, the biologist Elvi Okoye carries the network’s controller into a sphere of something that kills alien machines, and the defences fall silent. Murtry is taken for trial.
Naomi taken — Naomi tries to disable the corporate shuttle Murtry has rigged as a bomb and is captured aboard the Edward Israel. Alex aims the Rocinante’s railgun at the Israel’s reactor.
Blindness — In the ruins, a tiny organism in the rainwater starts to blind the colonists. Holden’s daily anti-cancer drugs protect him, Elvi works out why, and he gives his supply away.
Under Ilus — Miller, riding a huge alien machine, leads Holden down into the planet’s transit network and explains what Ilus was built for.
On the bridge — Murtry follows them down and shoots Amos from behind, and the RCE officer Wei is killed. On a narrow bridge, Holden shoots Murtry and drags him to safety.
Goodbye, Miller — With a new town rising on Ilus, Holden sends the protomolecule fragment that carried Miller into Ilus’s sun.
The Callisto raid — A radical Belter cell, led by a teenager named Filip, steals stealth coating from the Callisto shipyards and wrecks them.
Shore leave — With the Rocinante under repair at Tycho, the crew scatters. Holden takes up a journalist’s question: who is stealing colony ships?
Alex and Bobbie — Alex goes home to Mars and teams up with Bobbie, who is chasing missing Martian warships. Someone tries to kill them both.
Naomi’s past — Naomi answers a call from her past on Ceres: her son Filip, and his father, Marco Inaros. Marco takes her prisoner.
The rocks fall — Marco’s Free Navy drops stealth-coated asteroids on Earth. The strikes and what follows kill vast numbers and break the planet.
Tycho attacked — In the same coordinated strike the Free Navy hits Tycho and steals the last sample of the protomolecule.
Medina seized — Free Navy ships seize Medina Station and close the gates.
The stolen fleet — Alex and Bobbie find the hidden fleet of stolen Martian warships, then save the Martian prime minister from an ambush and carry him to Luna in Bobbie’s racing yacht.
Off the ground — Amos breaks Clarissa out of prison. With his old friend Erich they make their way through the wreckage and fly to Luna from a rich enclave’s launch pad.
Survivors — Naomi slips Marco’s trap and is picked up by Alex and Bobbie. The crew comes together on Luna, where Avasarala is now acting Secretary-General.

A mole on Tycho — The journalist Monica Stuart, who has evidence of colony ships vanishing, is kidnapped; Holden and Fred find her sealed in a shipping container. Tycho’s chief engineer turns out to be a radical mole.

Naomi’s leap — Marco rigs the Chetzemoka as a bomb, with a false distress call in Naomi’s voice. She crosses open vacuum without a suit to reach it and turns the call into a coded message that she is alive.
Ceres abandoned — Marco strips Ceres and pulls out, leaving millions for his enemies to feed.
Michio Pa breaks away — Michio Pa, sickened by Marco’s methods, turns her ships to piracy for the Belt, seizing the colony ship Minsky on its way to San Esteban, and pays for it.
Retaking Medina — A combined fleet of Earth, Mars and the loyal Belt strikes for Medina. With its railguns silenced, Holden bluffs a full invasion, and the station surrenders to the Rocinante.
Marco vanishes — Naomi has worked out the rule of the vanishing ships. Mass sent through the Ring just ahead of Marco’s fleet makes the whole fleet disappear in the crossing.
The Transport Union — After the war, Holden proposes a union of Belter shippers to run the ring gates.
A joint fleet — On Luna, Avasarala, the Martian prime minister and Fred Johnson join forces against the Free Navy. Holden agrees to help if he keeps the Rocinante, with Bobbie as mission commander.
The guns fall — Bobbie leads the assault that silences the Free Navy’s slow-zone railguns.
Freehold — Some thirty years on, with Camina Drummer president of the Transport Union, the Rocinante is sent to make Freehold give up the governor who broke the Union’s rules.
Laconia’s fleet — On Laconia, Duarte’s people have used the builders’ orbital platforms and the protomolecule to build warships beyond anything in human space.
The Tempest comes — The battleship Heart of the Tempest comes through the Laconia gate, tears apart the slow zone’s defences and takes Medina. Captain Santiago Singh becomes governor.
The fleets broken — At Point Leuctra in the asteroid belt, the combined fleet fails to stop the Tempest.
Pallas destroyed — After Tycho’s section withdraws, the Tempest destroys Pallas Station.

The breakout — Saba frees the prisoners; Bobbie and Amos take the gunship Gathering Storm while ships flee through the gates. Clarissa dies after saving Naomi, and Singh is shot by his own security chief.
Hiding on Freehold — The Rocinante escapes the ring space and hides on Freehold.
A Laconian governor — Auberon is one of the first colonies to accept the new order, and Duarte sends it a governor.
Duarte — Holden arrives on Laconia as a prisoner and meets High Consul Duarte, who means to use the protomolecule to rule humanity and live forever.
Singh’s rule — After an assassination attempt kills his aide, Singh clamps curfews on Medina and removes his security chief, Colonel Aliana Tanaka, when she objects.
Avasarala’s funeral — Chrisjen Avasarala dies of old age and is given a state funeral on Laconia. Holden, still a captive, pays his respects.
The diamond — Elvi Okoye’s Laconian science ship Falcon explores the dead systems and finds a vast green crystal that reacts to the protomolecule.
Thanjavur cut off — The burst through the slow zone destroys the gate to Thanjavur, stranding its colony.
The ring space wiped clean — The ring entities answer. Everyone everywhere blacks out; in the ring space, Medina Station and the battleship Typhoon are destroyed. Only the Falcon gets out.
The empty throne — Duarte, changed by the protomolecule, is left senseless by the attack. His court hides it. Elvi is put to work on him and learns how the native repair creatures restore the dead.
Timothy — Teresa Duarte’s secret friend in the hills is Amos, sent to get Holden out. Laconian security kills him, and his body disappears.
Naomi takes command — Stranded when the gates close, Naomi reaches Auberon and takes over its Underground.

The siege of Laconia — Naomi leads hundreds of ships through the Laconia gate. While they draw off the last flagship, a strike force destroys the orbital construction platforms, so Laconia can build no more.
The freighter — In the stolen Gathering Storm, Bobbie and Alex take a Laconian freighter near Jupiter. The political officer aboard dies in the crossfire, and Bobbie finds antimatter in the hold.
Teresa — Duarte begins to train his fourteen-year-old daughter Teresa as his heir. She slips out of the palace to visit a man in a mountain cave whom she calls Timothy.
Duarte wakes — Duarte wakes and kills Cortázar. Teresa leaves with Holden using Amos’s beacon, Amos returns changed, and the Rocinante crew is together again.
The hunt for Duarte — Duarte walks out of the State Building and vanishes in a small alien ship. Colonel Aliana Tanaka traces him through Amos’s old cave and sets out after Teresa.
New Egypt — Tanaka’s marines are waiting when the Rocinante brings Teresa to New Egypt. In the firefight Amos is shot, and keeps going.
Draper Station — At the Underground’s base a local leader tries to trade the crew to Laconia for peace. Tanaka storms the station, and the Gathering Storm is lost covering the Rocinante’s escape.
San Esteban dies — The ring entities change the laws of physics in the San Esteban system and nearly every living thing there dies.
Bara Gaon — Tanaka follows the wrong ship to Bara Gaon and, on its fifth planet, gets help for her wounds and the memories that are not hers.
Diving the diamond — At Adro, Elvi’s team and the crew send Cara and Amos into the diamond’s memory and learn how the builders lived and died.
The rings shine — A colony ship crossing from Sol too soon after another should vanish, but something saves it. Every ring glows, minds touch, and the attacks stop.

The last battle — Duarte has joined himself to the Ring Station, pulling minds into a single will to hold the dark gods back. In the station’s heart Tanaka kills him and dies; Holden, dying of the protomolecule he took to get in, takes Duarte’s place.
Alex’s last flight — The crew parts. Alex takes the Rocinante to Nieuwestad, where his son’s family lives.
The gates close — Once the ring space is clear, Holden destroys the station. The gates die with it, and some thirteen hundred colonies are on their own.
The Thirty Worlds — About a thousand years later, a federation of colonies has built its own faster-than-light ship and sets out to find old Earth.

Opening the station — Duarte’s small ship is found on the Ring Station’s surface. Teresa, Tanaka and Amos come to open the station; Holden injects himself with live protomolecule to follow, and Miller appears once more.
Battle in the slow zone — Laconian and Underground ships fight side by side to hold off the crews Duarte has taken over, while the struggle inside the station goes on.
The Underground’s base in the Freehold system (shown on the world for convenience; marker position schematic).
The crew runs for the Rocinante and escapes through the gate, while the Gathering Storm sacrifices itself to cover them.
The resistance member Jillian Houston locks up the Rocinante’s crew and accepts Laconia’s offer of an armistice in exchange for Teresa. When Tanaka kills her guards, Jillian lets the crew go.
The colony’s only town, in a semi-arid temperate zone, run by its Assembly and a citizen militia (position estimated).
Freehold’s colonists govern themselves here. Facing a three-year trade ban from the Transport Union, they hand over their governor, Payne Houston, rather than starve.
After the breakout from Medina, the crew hides the Rocinante here, out of Laconia’s sight.
The farms under domes and mirrors (marker position estimated). Prax Meng is a botanist here, and his work is lost when a mirror comes down in the fighting.
The domed farms that feed the outer planets. Prax Meng works here as a botanist until the fighting brings down a mirror and his crops die.
Great mirrors that light the crops. One falls in the fighting, and the colony’s food system begins to collapse.
Four-year-old Mei Meng, who has an immune disorder, is taken from here by her own doctor just before the fighting starts. Other children with her condition vanish too.
A disused tunnel complex (position estimated) where Mei’s doctor takes her. Holden, Amos and Prax find it, and one of the monsters inside.
Inside the lab a transformed human is held in a cage, the kind of creature that killed Bobbie’s platoon. A ship lifts off during the fighting, and Prax fears Mei is aboard.
Holden, Amos and Prax follow video of the kidnapping through these tunnels to a guarded secret lab, and fight their way in.
Where a single creature in no armour kills Bobbie Draper’s Martian platoon and the UN marines facing them (position estimated).
Martian and UN marines watch each other across the surface. A creature with no suit walks out of the UN side and kills them all except Bobbie, then destroys itself.
Among the rocks (marker position schematic): where the stolen Martian warships wait.
A fleet of Martian warships missing from the navy’s books, hidden among the asteroids. Alex and Bobbie find them in the racing ship Razorback and flee under missile fire.
A gap in the planet’s network, a sphere of something that kills alien machines. Elvi carries the network’s controller into it and shuts down the defences.
Dormant machines wake and attack as Elvi pulls Miller’s core free. Fayez Sarkis attacks Murtry so she can run deeper.
A darkness at the heart of the network that only Elvi can perceive. Miller asks her to carry his core into it; she does, is taken apart and put back together, and the alien machines fall silent.
The three ships above the planet: the Rocinante, the corporate Edward Israel and the refugees’ ore ship Barbapiccola (marker position schematic).

The refugees’ ore ship, falling with its reactor dead. Naomi tries to tow it up with the Rocinante’s railgun recoil; the tether is cut, and Basia gets the crew out in improvised pods before it burns up.
Royal Charter Energy’s survey ship, home of Murtry’s security team. Naomi is captured aboard trying to disable a shuttle rigged as a bomb, until Havelock turns on Murtry and frees her.
Alex holds the ship in orbit on battery power. At the end Holden sends the protomolecule fragment that held Miller into Ilus’s sun.
One of the alien reactors in the archipelago melts down here, throwing up a tsunami and storm winds that flatten First Landing.
An alien power plant under the island chain explodes. The blast raises hurricane winds, and the planet’s defences shut down every fusion reactor in orbit.

The refugee town, just north of the great south-western desert, where the lithium is closest to the surface. The colonists bomb the corporate landing pad here, and the feud begins (all Ilus positions estimated).
Doctor Lucia Merton, Basia’s wife, leads the medical care for the town after the bombing and through the disasters that follow.
The reason the refugees came: lithium close to the surface near the edge of the desert.

Built by Royal Charter Energy’s advance team. Basia Merton and the other colonists plant bombs under it; when the corporate shuttle comes down early he can stop only one of the detonators, and the provisional governor and a dozen others die.
The settlement the Ganymede refugees built to mine lithium. When a colonist threatens him in public, the corporate security chief Murtry shoots the man dead here.
Builder ruins near the town, where survivors shelter from the storm and the poisonous slugs, and where Holden and Miller ride an alien car into the planet’s machinery.
Deep in the structure, after Murtry shoots Amos from behind and the RCE officer Wei is killed, Holden faces Murtry, shoots him and drags him to safety.
The town’s survivors shelter here from the storm. A tiny organism in the rainwater starts to blind them; Holden is spared by his anti-cancer medicine and gives his supply away.

Guided by Miller, who has taken over a huge alien machine, Holden travels down into the planet’s old transit network. Miller explains that Ilus was built to process rare minerals and send power across worlds.
A hidden base (position estimated) where Mei and other immune-deficient children are held. Amos and Prax get her out while Holden and the fleets fight overhead.
Where the surviving children are kept. Prax finds Mei alive.
Bobbie, Prax and Amos land here. Bobbie holds off another hybrid outside while the others go in.
The workrooms of the doctor who took Mei. Amos kills him here.
The space above Io (marker position schematic), where the UN ships of Nguyen and Souther face each other.
Admiral Nguyen refuses to surrender and launches hybrid-loaded rockets. One crashes into his own ship and infects those aboard; Holden boards it to get the tracking codes, and the ship is destroyed.
UN ships under Admiral Souther, working with Avasarala to stop the release of the protomolecule.
The crowded space among Jupiter’s moons, busy with traffic between its colonies (marker position schematic).
A supply ship carrying a senior Laconian political officer. Bobbie and Alex take it in the stolen gunship Gathering Storm, and find antimatter aboard.
Ships sent by the rogue faction to kill Holden. With Martian warships on its side and Bobbie on the guns, the Rocinante beats them.
Jules-Pierre Mao’s private yacht, the Guanshiyin, on which Avasarala is sent out of the way. When she learns ships are coming to kill Holden, Bobbie takes the yacht by force.
Where Teresa Duarte secretly visits a man she calls Timothy, who is really Amos Burton. He is killed in a firefight here, and the native repair creatures bring him back.
Teresa sneaks out to meet a man here she calls Timothy. He is Amos, sent with a pocket nuclear weapon to free Holden. Laconian security kills him, and his body vanishes.
Tracking the vanished High Consul, Colonel Tanaka finds that he came to Amos’s old cave and left in a small alien ship.
The builders’ huge construction platforms in orbit over Laconia, where Duarte’s warships are grown (marker position schematic).
Alien construction platforms that Laconia controls with protomolecule samples, growing warships no one else can match.
Naomi’s hundreds of ships draw out the last flagship guarding Laconia while a strike force destroys the platforms. Laconia is left with one flagship and no way to build more.
Cortázar’s research facility, where Elvi meets the children Cara and Xan, brought back from death by the planet’s native repair creatures.
Brought in to cure Duarte, Elvi learns here that his long life came from two dead children rebuilt by Laconia’s native repair drones.
The Duarte family’s seat in the capital of the Laconian Empire, where Holden is held as a prisoner-guest (all Laconia positions estimated).
Holden is brought here as a prisoner. Duarte visits him and offers an alliance: humanity must meet whatever killed the builders with discipline, under one ruler.
Holden may walk the palace grounds but never leave, and he is always watched. He speaks with Kajri, Avasarala’s granddaughter, and with Drummer at Avasarala’s wake.
Chrisjen Avasarala dies of old age and is given a state funeral on Laconia; Holden, still a captive, pays his respects.
Left senseless when the ring entities strike, Duarte lies here while Trejo, Ilich, Teresa and Cortázar hide his condition. When he wakes he kills Cortázar.
The fourteen-year-old heir is being trained to succeed a father who means never to die. She slips out to the hills, and in the end leaves with Holden using Amos’s beacon.
A schematic marker for the battle in the Belt; the books do not tie it to a body.
The ships of Earth, Mars and the Transport Union, gathered to stop the Heart of the Tempest. They fail.
Where the surviving governments of Earth and Mars gather after the rocks fall, and Avasarala runs the war against the Free Navy (marker position estimated).
Acting Secretary-General Avasarala meets Fred Johnson, the Martian prime minister and Holden’s crew here. Naomi offers testimony in exchange for immunity.
Survivors come in here: Alex and Bobbie bring the Martian prime minister in the Razorback, and Amos, Clarissa and Erich land after escaping Earth.
Avasarala, the Martian prime minister and Fred Johnson plan the strike on the Azure Dragon here, and later send the fleets to retake Ceres.
A volcano with a training base for Martian marine special forces.
One of Mars’s major cities (its position on the planet is not given; marker estimated).
A great settlement built along the canyon walls of Valles Marineris, its neighbourhoods linked by tubes across the canyon, with shipyards nearby. Alex Kamal’s home.
Alex grew up in Mariner Valley. He comes back in the fifth book hoping to make peace with his ex-wife, and she turns him away.
Neighbourhoods dug into the canyon walls, joined by tubes that cross the gorge.
Martian shipyards near the valley.
The great volcano, with settlements and a Martian navy base on its flanks.
The great ship turned station: the spinning habitat drum, the engineering decks and the bridge, parked in the slow zone (marker position schematic).
Ashford orders the laser fired from here. Clarissa, moved by Anna’s broadcast, opens the doors, knocks Ashford from the controls and sends the ship dark.
Clarissa is held here after her attack on the Rocinante. Anna visits her and offers forgiveness she will not accept; Ashford plots his comeback from a cell.
The Laconian gunship Gathering Storm is berthed here. In the breakout Bobbie’s team seizes it and Alex takes the Rocinante out, as twenty ships escape through the gates.
Captain Santiago Singh rules Medina from here for Laconia, with curfews and purges. His own security chief, Overstreet, kills him when he orders loyalists executed.
Ashford has the ship’s communications laser turned into a weapon to strike the Ring. Holden fears the station will answer by destroying the Sun.
Where the Rocinante tries to leave Teresa Duarte in safety (marker position estimated).
The crew fights its way back to the Rocinante. Amos is shot and keeps going.
A boarding school where the crew means to leave Teresa. Tanaka and her Laconian marines are already waiting.
Where Alex’s son Kit and his family live (marker position estimated).
At the end of the series Alex flies the Rocinante here to join his son and grandchild.
The station on the asteroid, with its refineries and the joined Tycho section (marker position schematic).
The industry of Pallas, among the largest in the Belt. The Tempest destroys the station.
Tycho Station, moved and joined to Pallas in the decades since the sixth book. It withdraws before the Tempest strikes.
The moon’s interior, where the alien cargo lay hidden (marker position schematic).
Where Protogen found the protomolecule: a payload sent at the young Earth billions of years ago and caught by Saturn instead.
The Ring Station at the centre of the slow zone, where Holden goes in alone with Miller’s ghost in the third book and touches the station’s memory.
Inside, Miller’s ghost shows Holden the builders’ empire across the galaxy, the thing that attacked it, and the systems they burned to stop it. To be judged harmless, every ship must power down.
A glowing metal sphere a few kilometres across at the centre of the ring space. Believing Miller has called him, Holden makes a solo spacewalk to it.
Laconian scientists find Duarte’s small alien ship resting on the Ring Station’s surface. Teresa, Tanaka and Amos come here to open the station, and Miller appears once more to help.
In the last book Duarte sits here, joined to the station, holding humanity’s minds together against the dark gods. Tanaka kills him and dies; Holden takes his place.
The dark sphere of the ring space, with its gates on the rim (marker position schematic).
Laconian and Underground fleets hold off the ships whose crews Duarte has taken over, while the struggle goes on at the station.
When a Martian marine fires a grenade near the station, the speed limit drops at a stroke, and every ship in the zone is slammed to a crawl. Hundreds are killed or hurt.
1,373 gates spaced around the edge of the million-kilometre sphere, each opening onto another star system once the station unlocks them.
The railguns that guard the slow zone for the Free Navy; where they are mounted is schematic here.
Two gates on opposite sides of the rim. The gamma-ray burst from the Tecoma experiment crosses the slow zone and destroys both.
San Esteban’s settlement (marker position estimated; the books give no detail of its towns).
The destination of the colony ship Minsky, seized on its way here by Michio Pa’s breakaway ships.
The ring entities shift the laws of physics here; chemistry fails and nearly every living thing in the system dies.
Saturn’s rings, where ice haulers load water for the Belt (marker position schematic).
An old ice hauler that carries water from Saturn’s rings to Ceres. Jim Holden is its executive officer and Naomi Nagata, Amos Burton and Alex Kamal are among its crew.
The space in front of the gate, where the navies watch and ships line up to cross (marker position schematic).
Ships line up here to cross into the ring space. The coalition times a heavily loaded ship’s transit against Marco Inaros’s fleet as it crosses, and his whole fleet vanishes in the gate.
Earth, Mars and the OPA send fleets to watch the Ring. Clarissa Mao’s bomb destroys the Earth destroyer Seung Un here, and the Behemoth fires on the Rocinante until Holden flies into the gate.

A dark ring about a thousand kilometres across. Manéo Jung-Espinoza, a young Belter from Ceres, slingshots a patched-up ship through it; on the far side it stops dead and kills him, but his camera keeps broadcasting.
Thanjavur’s settlement (marker position estimated; the books give no detail of it).
A human colony that loses its only gate when the Tecoma burst crosses the slow zone, cutting it off from everyone else for good.
Protogen’s hidden base, where the Eros data comes in (marker position schematic).
OPA fighters, Holden’s crew and Miller fight their way through the station.
The station’s research heart. Antony Dresden defends the Eros experiment as a step toward making humanity into gods, and Miller shoots him.
Badly damaged in the fight with the station’s defences, the Rocinante is forced to set down on Thoth itself.
The station itself: a manufacturing sphere wrapped in spinning habitat rings, with berths for the largest ships in the system (marker position schematic).
The Rocinante is repaired here after the battle at Thoth, while the crew plans what to do about Eros.
Fred runs the station and his wing of the OPA from here. He takes in Holden’s crew after the Donnager and hires them for OPA work.
Where the Nauvoo, the largest ship ever built, is under construction as a generation ship for Mormon colonists. The OPA takes it to try to push Eros into the Sun.
The spinning rings where Tycho’s workers live, with gravity from the spin.
Where Fred keeps the last known sample of the protomolecule. During the fifth book’s coup attempt, insurgents steal the safe.
The heart of the station, where Tycho Manufacturing builds ships too big for anyone else to build.
The crash site of Eros Station (position estimated; the books give none). From here the protomolecule spreads out under the clouds and begins to build.
Where Eros comes down under the clouds at the end of the first book, carrying Miller and what is left of Julie.
Vast shapes grow across the surface after the crash, and no government can say what they are for. At the end of the second book the construction lifts off and leaves the planet.

head_text: Kassad among the Tombs — After Bressia, Kassad’s ship is attacked in the Hyperion system. He comes down near the Time Tombs, meets Moneta in the flesh, and fights the Ousters there with her.
The City of Poets — Silenus follows Sad King Billy’s artists to Hyperion. When the Shrike killings empty the city he stays on alone, writing the Cantos.
Across the Sea of Grass — From Edge a windwagon carries them over the grass sea. Het Masteen disappears, leaving his erg behind.
The Scholar’s Tale — Sol tells how Rachel caught Merlin’s sickness studying the Tombs, and now grows younger every day.
Abraham’s dream — Sol dreams of a voice telling him to take his daughter to Hyperion, as Abraham was told to take Isaac to the mountain.
The Detective’s Tale — Lamia recounts her case for Johnny, the Keats cybrid. Lamia and Johnny investigate his death and reach a replica of Old Earth.
The trail to Madhya — Lamia and Johnny’s investigation leads them to Madhya.
Over the Bridle Range — The pilgrims restart the old cable car and cross the mountains.
Siri and Merin — A starship crewman, Merin Aspic returns to Maui-Covenant every few years of local time while barely ageing, so his love affair with Siri spans her whole life.
Rebellion on Maui-Covenant — As the farcaster that will join Maui-Covenant to the Web nears completion, Merin sabotages it and rebellion breaks out. FORCE crushes the uprising.
Night at Chronos Keep — In the deserted Shrike Church fortress, the pilgrims choose to go on together.
War council — Gladstone and the second Keats cybrid, Joseph Severn, follow the pilgrims through his dreams as FORCE gathers against the Ousters.
Kassad and Moneta — Kassad fights Moneta and the Shrike across the Tombs and is pulled through time.
Silenus on the Tree — Silenus goes back to the Poets’ City to finish the Cantos and is taken to the Tree of Thorns.
Lamia in the megasphere — Attacked near Chronos Keep, Lamia finds Johnny again inside the Core, where the AI Ummon explains the war of the Ultimate Intelligences.
The hidden farcaster — FORCE moves its fleets through a concealed military farcaster near Madhya during the war.
God’s Grove burns — Duré and Gladstone are on the Templar world as it goes up in flames; Duré barely farcasts out.
Duré becomes Pope — The College of Cardinals elects Duré as Pope Teilhard I.
Severn dies in Rome — A farcaster sends Severn to the Core’s copy of Earth, where he dies of tuberculosis just as Keats did.
The Consul meets the Ousters — The Consul flies out to the Swarm and learns the Core has been staging the war.
Gladstone’s death — Gladstone walks out alone to meet the rioting crowd and is killed.
Kassad’s last battle — In Hyperion’s far future Kassad leads the charge against the Shrike legions and dies; he is laid in the Crystal Monolith.
Lamia frees Silenus — Lamia goes into the Shrike Palace and brings Silenus back from the Tree.
Raul is recruited — Framed and condemned, Raul is rescued and given a mission by the ancient Silenus: protect Aenea, find Old Earth, bring down the Pax.
De Soya’s commission — On Pacem, Father Captain de Soya is given the archangel Raphael and papal authority to bring back a girl who will step out of the Sphinx.
Into the Tethys — Aenea brings the ship down on Renaissance Vector, then flies it through a dormant Tethys farcaster.
A raft on the river — With the ship damaged, they build a raft and float the River Tethys from world to world.
Nemes joins the hunt — Resurrected yet again, de Soya is given a new crew member by Lourdusamy: the Core-made Rhadamanth Nemes.
The sea platform — Raul runs explosives past a Pax platform on the hawking mat, is wounded, and loses the mat.
Father Glaucus — In a city sealed under the ice, the blind exiled priest Father Glaucus takes the travellers in.
The ice world — Father Glaucus and the Chitchatuk shelter them on frozen Sol Draconi Septem; Nemes later kills them all.
Ambush on God’s Grove — Nemes ambushes the party and Bettik loses an arm. The Shrike fights her and de Soya fires on her from orbit so Aenea can escape.
Old Earth — The last portal opens on a living Earth in the Magellanic Cloud. They travel from Fallingwater to Taliesin West.
Taliesin West — Aenea settles in to study architecture at Taliesin West under the Old Architect, a cybrid of Frank Lloyd Wright.
A crusade is proclaimed — Hoyt, now Pope Urban XVI, proclaims a crusade against the Ousters.
Aenea sends Raul away — After four years at Taliesin and the Old Architect’s death, sixteen-year-old Aenea sends Raul down the Tethys by kayak to fetch the Consul’s ship.
De Soya recalled — After the failure of his first hunt, de Soya has spent years in exile on his home world before the Pax calls him back to service.
The Grand Inquisitor on Mars — Cardinal Mustafa, the Grand Inquisitor, travels to Mars to investigate massacres blamed on the Shrike.
Fever on Vitus — Raul collapses with a kidney stone and is sheltered by the Amoiete Spectrum Helix. The Shrike saves him from Core assassins.
Inside the gas giant — Deep in the Outback, a giant zeplin-like creature swallows Raul, and he lives.
The ship, repaired — Raul finds the Consul’s ship mended and waiting, and sets out for T’ien Shan.
Aenea’s travels — Over five years Aenea teaches and builds on Ixion, Maui-Covenant, Renaissance Vector, Patawpha, Amritsar and Groombridge Dyson D.
First circles on Ixion — Aenea’s first stop after Old Earth: she helps rebuild Ixion’s cities and holds her first discussion circles.
The Great Wall — Aenea and her companions work on Groombridge Dyson D’s wall-city, where A. Bettik meets other androids of his kind.
Tree houses on Maui-Covenant — On a rebel-held motile isle, Aenea learns to build tree houses.
Building on Patawpha — Aenea builds houses among the trees of Patawpha’s swamp forests.
Tents on Amritsar — Aenea builds tent homes for nomadic Sikh and Sufi bands on the desert world, and meets a later Rachel Weintraub.
Reunion on T’ien Shan — Raul arrives after five years’ time debt. He and Aenea become lovers, and she begins her communion of shared blood.
Battle of T’ien Shan — Pax forces and the Nemes clones attack. Admiral Wu is killed and the Shrike intervenes.
Freecast to the Startree — Aenea freecasts the ship through the Void to the Startree, where Raul learns that the cruciform and the Core feed on human minds.
The Biosphere burns — The Pax fleet destroys much of the Startree. Aenea saves survivors on a treeship and sends disciples out to many worlds.
Martyrdom on Pacem — Aenea confronts the Pope, is tortured by Nemes and burned to death. The Shared Moment reaches nearly every human mind.
Out of the cat box — Imprisoned above Armaghast, Raul learns to freecast and escapes.
A new pope — With the Core’s hold broken, Paul Duré, alive again, becomes pope once more.
